title: Family Resource Worker
description: ## POSITION SUMMARY: The Family Resource Worker at Western Ottawa Community Resource Centre coordinates and delivers programs and services that support the needs of parents / care providers and children birth to 6 years in the communities of Kanata, West Carleton and Stittsville. The position supports the Centre-wide and strategic level health promotion and community development activities, including community assessments and program evaluation activities. This a full-time permanent position at 35 hours a week with an annual salary range of $49,313 to $51,306. This is a Monday - Friday rotation schedule with two evenings per week. ## PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES: ## Program Development and Delivery • Develop playgroups and activities for children • Promoting child development and encouraging parent/ care provider-child interaction; • Using the recreational resources available in the community; • Managing and coordinating the planning of the playgroups and activities; • Using modeling for the parent/ care provider in the relation with the child; • Ensuring the parent/care provider understands the reason and the impact of the activities; • Presenting activities in a dynamic and stimulating fashion for the child, in collaboration with the parent/care provider; • Ensuring integration and adaptation of children and parent/care providers. • Assist parent/care providers to increase their awareness of child development • Providing information and referral to parent/care providers; • Providing education services for parent/care providers through workshops and other training opportunities; • Supporting parent/care providers in identifying their needs; • Assisting parent/care providers to identify their strengths and limitations to help improve their child's and their own quality of life; • Linking and referring care providers to other programs offered by the CRC and other community organizations. • Coordinating and delivering early learning programs and services throughout our communities, including rural, in local schools and in the EYC; • Planning programs that will stimulate interest and curiosity through collaboration with parent/care providers, placement students and volunteers; • Providing support and training to volunteers as required; • Creating a sense of program ownership and engagement with parent/care providers as well as with partnering organizations • Developing, coordinating and delivering programs and services that are aligned with community needs, trends and gaps based on client feedback and data such as EDI and Census data as well as in consultation with partnering organizations; • Performing program evaluation in collaboration with participants, volunteers and partners; • Maintaining and developing professional competence and quality assurance through appropriate continuing education methods; to support both family resource worker and community development role and responsibilities; • Reporting data using the CRC data base (CIMS) to support funder reporting requirements; • Providing information for the web-site. ## Outreach, Connecting and Participating in the Community • Serve as ambassador to ensure that services are accessible, and the general public is informed regarding EYC services • Promoting participation of parent/care providers, and the community, in activities designated to educate and/or advocate for healthy child development; • Work in collaboration with the Communications department to develop promotional and marketing strategies to increase awareness of our programs and services • Participating in community groups regarding issues and services relevant to the 0- 6 population; • Contributing to the creation and distribution of materials and resources related to the activities of the EYC; • Establishing and maintaining links with community groups and agencies to facilitate a positive working relationship. ## Training, facilitation and event planning • Providing training to community groups and/or participating in community events to promote programs and services; • Preparing and presenting awareness training and care provider focused information sessions in partnership with other services; ## Other All WOCRC employees have some fundamental responsibilities that go beyond the confines of their occupations. These include: • Ensuring that the commitment to diversity is understood and respected. This includes diversity of culture, language, faith expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, socio-economic resources and degrees of physical (dis)ability; • Working in a manner that incorporates health promotion and recognizes the determinants of health • Maintaining up-to-date professional skills and knowledge through formal and informal training; • Acting as an "ambassador" for WOCRC within and outside the Centre by creating an awareness of WOCRC programs and promoting services offered; • Compliance with all mandated legal/regulatory requirements related to working at WOCRC (Employment Standards Act, Occupational Health and Safety, standards of professional conduct); • Maintaining awareness of and compliance with WOCRC policies and procedures; • Maintaining awareness of and compliance with funder requirements, policies, procedures and regulations; • Working in a manner that preserves confidentiality and seeks to minimize risk in keeping with Privacy and Confidentiality Policies and Procedures; • Supporting the Centre's student and volunteer placement programs; • Working during both regular and extended hours of operation in locations identified by the Centre; • Perform other related duties as assigned ## QUALIFICATIONS: ## Education and Experience: • Post-secondary diploma in early childhood education with registration at the College of Early Childhood Educators • Two years' experience in an early learning environment, working with children, parents and care providers. • Experience working in partnership with other early years providers in a service integration framework. • Knowledge of the day nurseries act • Knowledge of Ontario Early years Framework • Knowledge of Early training for Every Child today (ELECT) • Knowledge of "How does Learning Happen" Pedagogy • First Aid and CPR training • Experience with and sensitivity to minority groups, people of different age and income groups and an awareness of the issues that affect rural populations ## Competencies: • Demonstrated ability to work independently in remote locations • Demonstrated autonomy and initiative • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills • Demonstrated ability to work in a multi-cultural, multi-disciplinary team environment • Demonstrated ability to work within an Equity inclusion framework ## Language: • Ability to communicate fluently in English, spoken and written. • Ability to communicate fluently in French, spoken and written, an asset. • Other languages reflective of the community we serve an asset. ## Computer Competencies: • Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office suite of products • Familiarity with Data Management Systems ## Other: • Valid driver's license and access to a vehicle required with valid insurance. • Requirement to work flexible hours (daytime, evenings, and weekends)

title: Manager, Maintenance and Trades
description: Facilities proudly builds, maintains and improves campus facilities to create a safe and welcoming environment in support of teaching, learning and research. Reporting to the Assistant Director, Operations and Maintenance, the Manager, Maintenance and Trades (Manager), is an integral member of the Facilities operations management team and Facilities leadership team that is committed to a reputation as a trusted client focused service provider to the university community. The Manager provides campus-wide leadership for the university's centralized trades and technical services team and is responsible for the safe, reliable and efficient delivery of specialized maintenance, repair and technical services across the university's buildings and infrastructure. The portfolio includes electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning, refrigeration, building automation and controls, millwright, carpentry, door and lock systems, and other specialized building services. Working closely with Area Managers, Building Operators, Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, Energy and Sustainability, and Fixit Client Services, the Manager ensures that specialized work is properly prioritized, planned, assigned, completed and documented through the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS). While the Area Managers and Building Operators retain responsibility for building-level ownership, routine inspections and first-level maintenance, the Manager leads the centralized technical resources required for specialized, licensed, complex or higher-risk work. With a strategic results driven approach, the Manager establishes consistent technical standards, strengthens preventive maintenance and regulatory compliance, improves equipment reliability, and champions an inclusive service-oriented trades team that celebrates the diversity of others and where team members take pride in their work and their contribution to the mission of Facilities and the university. In addition, Manager participates in establishing long term goals and is responsible for providing leadership and expertise on strategic initiatives and policies, as well as contributing to their development, implementation, and related communication, and will ensure that proposed solutions meet stakeholder needs through ongoing assessment of process and deliverables. The Manager must be available to respond to emergency calls outside of normal working hours. In addition, the Manager works an assigned shift and is on a rotating call-in list for emergency calls from the Emergency Response Centre. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Maintenance Planning and Work Execution • Lead the intake, assessment, prioritization, planning, scheduling and assignment of specialized trades work received through the CMMS. • Ensure that work is directed to the appropriate internal trade, technical specialist or external contractor. • Establish service priorities based on health and safety, regulatory compliance, life safety, operational impact, asset criticality and client requirements. • Monitor preventive and corrective maintenance backlogs, response times, work completion, overtime, contractor use and recurring equipment failures. • Ensure completed work orders include accurate labour, material, asset, failure and corrective-action information. • Establish key performance indicators and use maintenance and asset data to identify trends, improve planning and address recurring problems through root-cause analysis. • Develop consistent maintenance procedures, job plans, inspection requirements and quality-control practices. • Ensure temporary repairs are documented, monitored and followed by permanent corrective action. Technical and Regulatory Oversight • Provide technical leadership for building mechanical, electrical, refrigeration, controls and related systems within the assigned portfolio. • Ensure work is completed in accordance with applicable legislation, regulations, codes, standards, manufacturer requirements and university policies. • Support compliance associated with TSSA-regulated equipment, refrigeration systems, pressure vessels, electrical systems, fuel-burning equipment and other regulated building systems. • Ensure required inspections, tests, maintenance activities, licences, certificates and operating records are current, complete and readily available. • Work with Engineering, Environmental Health and Safety, the Central Heating Plant and other technical authorities to clarify requirements and address identified risks. • Immediately escalate to the Assistant Director, unsafe conditions, overdue regulatory work and significant equipment risks. • Participate in investigations involving equipment failures, service disruptions, safety incidents and regulatory concerns. • Review and audit technical work completed by employees and contractors to confirm quality, completeness and compliance. Preventive Maintenance and Asset Reliability • Strengthen preventive, predictive and condition-based maintenance programs for critical building systems. • Review equipment history, failure patterns and maintenance performance to improve reliability and reduce unplanned downtime. • Establish critical-equipment priorities and support the development of contingency and business-continuity plans. • Work with Engineering and Asset Management to identify aging infrastructure, deferred maintenance and renewal priorities. • Participate in equipment selection, commissioning, project turnover and the transfer of new assets into operations. • Ensure operating and maintenance information, warranties, spare-parts requirements and preventive maintenance procedures are captured before project closeout. • Support energy-efficient equipment operation and collaborate on initiatives that reduce utility consumption and greenhouse-gas emissions without compromising safety or service. Operational Coordination and Client Service • Work closely with Area Managers and Building Operators to define service responsibilities and ensure effective escalation of specialized work. • Provide technical advice during complex building problems, occupant comfort concerns, equipment failures and service interruptions. • Coordinate planned outages and major maintenance activities with affected departments and campus partners. • Ensure clients receive timely, clear and accurate information regarding work status, operational impacts and expected completion. • Establish service expectations between the centralized trades team and campus operating areas. • Collaborate with Fixit Client Service to improve work-order quality, scheduling, requester notifications and performance reporting. • Participate in emergency response and recovery activities affecting university facilities. Contractor, Financial and Resource Management • Determine when work should be completed by internal resources or external contractors based on capacity, competency, risk, urgency and value. • Develop scopes of work, review quotations and provide technical input into procurement and contract-award processes. • Oversee contractor performance, safety, quality, schedule, documentation and compliance with university requirements. • Develop and manage assigned operating budgets and support monthly forecasting and variance reporting. • Monitor overtime, materials, service contracts and contractor expenditures. • Identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce avoidable costs and make better use of internal technical resources. • Maintain appropriate tools, equipment, vehicles, materials and critical spare-parts inventories. Health and Safety • Demonstrate visible leadership and accountability for health and safety. • Ensure work is properly planned and performed in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act and university policies and procedures. • Confirm that required hazard assessments, permits, isolation procedures and safe-work plans are completed. • Maintain effective programs for lockout/tagout, confined-space entry, hot work, working at heights, electrical safety, refrigerant management and other applicable hazards. • Investigate incidents and near misses and ensure corrective actions are completed. • Exercise stop-work authority where an unsafe condition or activity is identified. Leadership and People Management • Provide direct leadership to a multidisciplinary team of licensed tradespeople, technical specialists, apprentices and other assigned employees. • Establish clear roles, performance expectations, service standards and accountability across the centralized trades team. • Plan and balance workloads based on operational risk, regulatory requirements, campus priorities and available resources. • Plan, prioritize and manage the work of employees, providing strategic and tactical advice, guidance and coaching. Identify the need for staff resources, participate on staffing committees, and make effective recommendations regarding employee selection. • Manage performance by establishing performance standards, reviewing and evaluating performance and conducting formal performance reviews on an ongoing basis. • Assess staff training and development needs, and ensure that employees receive training required to improve and sustain successful performance. • Investigate, address and resolve employee/labour relations issues, including disciplinary matters. Make decisions or effective recommendations on matters involving possible discipline, discharge and probationary termination. • Ensure employees maintain the licences, certifications and technical competencies required for their assigned work. • Promote collaboration, respectful workplace practices, continuous improvement and a strong service culture. • Support apprenticeship, technical training and professional development opportunities. • Coordinate after-hours coverage and provide leadership during operational emergencies, major equipment failures and planned shutdowns. ASSETS: • Professional Engineer, Certified Engineering Technologist, Certified Technician, relevant Red Seal trade certification or comparable professional designation. • Power Engineering or TSSA operating certification. • Facilities-management certification such as FMP, CFM, BOMI or equivalent. • Experience in a university, hospital, laboratory or similarly complex institutional environment. • Experience leading organizational change or implementing a centralized trades or building-operator model. • Training in project management, reliability-centred maintenance or asset management. SPECIAL SKILLS: • Promotes the value of diversity and the importance of being an inclusive organization and ensures equitable and fair treatment of others and actively works to make the workplace inclusive for all individuals. • Role models continual learning on the topics of equity and inclusivity. • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills (verbal and written) to develop and maintain strong relationships with a diverse range of individuals, including university facilities and operations managers, department managers, researchers, and administrators. • Broad technical understanding and the ability to lead employees from different trade disciplines. • Strong operational judgment and the ability to make timely decisions during emergencies and service disruptions. • Ability to prioritize competing demands using safety, compliance, operational impact and asset risk. • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use maintenance data to identify problems and improve performance. • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical audiences. • Strong relationship-management, conflict-resolution and performance-management skills. • Ability to establish accountability while maintaining a respectful, supportive and collaborative workplace. • Sound financial judgment and an understanding of public-sector stewardship. • Commitment to client service, continuous improvement and reliable campus operations. • Proficient administrative skills, including use of computers for data analysis, spreadsheets and word processing. Ability to adapt to and support implementation of new technologies. DECISION MAKING: • Takes equity and inclusivity into consideration when completing day to day tasks and decisions. Establishes priorities and assigns centralized technical resources. • Determines the appropriate trade, specialist or contractor required for assigned work. • Makes operational decisions during equipment failures and building emergencies. • Recommends equipment shutdowns where continued operation presents an unacceptable safety, compliance or asset risk. • Escalates significant regulatory, life-safety, operational and financial risks. • Approves overtime, materials and contractor expenditures within delegated authority. • Makes recommendations regarding staffing, training, equipment renewal, service contracts and operating budgets. • Contributes technical evidence and operational data to capital-planning and infrastructure-renewal decisions. • Establishes budgets and approves expenditures of funds. • Evaluates job candidates and make effective recommendations on suitable hires. • Makes decisions and/or effective recommendations regarding transfers and promotions. • Evaluates employee performance and decide on appropriate training or coaching to address lack of proficiency in carrying out responsibilities, or remedial action for staff disciplinary situations. • Assesses investigation outcome of grievances and makes effective recommendations on appropriate course of action or next steps on grievances. • Makes effective recommendations on level of discipline up to discharge and probationary termination. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: • University degree or college diploma in engineering, engineering technology, facilities management, building systems or a related discipline; or a recognized skilled-trade qualification combined with equivalent education and experience. • Greater than 7 years of progressively responsible experience managing the maintenance and operation of complex institutional, commercial or industrial facilities. • Demonstrated leadership experience supervising licensed tradespeople and technical employees across multiple disciplines. • Strong working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, HVAC, refrigeration, controls and building automation systems. • Experience managing in a unionized environment and applying collective agreements, organizational policies and established employment practices. • Demonstrated experience with preventive maintenance, asset reliability, regulatory compliance and maintenance planning. • Experience using a CMMS to plan work, manage backlogs, maintain asset records and measure performance. • Experience managing operating budgets, contractors, service agreements and procurement activities. • Working knowledge of relevant Ontario legislation, regulations, building and safety codes. • Capacity to be a competent supervisor within the meaning of the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act. • Valid Province of Ontario Full Class G driver's licence and insurable under the university's insurance plan. • Satisfactory criminal record check. • An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

title: Master's Scholarship Award for Women in Economics and Finance
description: ## Master's Scholarship Award for Women in Economics and Finance The Bank values the contributions of women in economics and finance and awards scholarships to support them in these specializations. This scholarship award also: • promotes the pursuit of graduate studies in Economics and Finance among women at the undergraduate level or those who have completed an undergraduate degree • proactively contributes to building a gender-balanced talent pool for the economics and finance professions in central banking These $10,000 CAD scholarships are awarded to female identifying candidates specializing in economics and finance. In addition to the award, successful candidates may be offered a work opportunity, with mentorship by a Bank employee. They may also be able to attend a learning event at the Bank related to central banking, economics or finance (e.g., lecture, conference, networking event). ## Eligibility Criteria Candidates in their final two years of an undergraduate program maintaining an average of 70 per cent or higher, or those who have completed an undergraduate degree with an overall average of 70 per cent or higher can apply. To be considered for the scholarship, you must: • be a Canadian citizen or Permanent Resident; • Self-identify as a woman. Note: applicants currently enrolled in a Master's program in Economics or Finance are not eligible to apply. ## Application Process For your application to be considered you must upload the following three mandatory documents: • Resume • Personal statement (500 words or less) that includes reflections on: • Your reason(s) for pursuing further education in Economics or Finance; and • What you are hoping to gain from this scholarship and work experience • Official or unofficial transcripts of undergraduate academic record to date; OR proof of completion of an undergraduate program with official transcript ## Application Deadline and Disbursement of Scholarships Applications and supporting documents must be received by September 27, 2026 23:59 EST. The $10,000 CAD is disbursed in a one instalment once the recipient shows proof of registration in a Master's Program in Economics or Finance at a degree granting institution. ## Additional information • English or French essential • Security level required: Reliability or Secret We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this scholarship. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.#

title: Student - EPIC Support

title: Bookkeeper and Administrative Assistant
description: ## Bookkeeper We are looking for a reliable, organized, and detail-oriented Bookkeeper to join our team. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys keeping financial records organized and wants to work in a great, supportive working environment with flexible hours. ## What We Offer • Flexible hours • Great working environment • Training and support for ESA and Hydro forms • A friendly and supportive team • Opportunity for a long-term position If you're an organized bookkeeper looking for flexibility and a positive work environment, we'd love to hear from you! ## Responsibilities • Update and maintain Accounts Payable (A/P) and Accounts Receivable (A/R) accounts • Tidy up and organize the books, ensuring financial records are accurate and up to date • Process payroll accurately and on time • Assist with year-end accounting preparation • Complete ESA and Hydro forms as required • Training will be provided • Maintain organized financial documentation and records • Assist with general bookkeeping and administrative tasks as needed • Maintain employee licenses, and health and safety records • • Other various tasks around the office ## What We're Looking For • Previous bookkeeping experience • Strong attention to detail and organization • Comfortable working with financial records and accounting software • Ability to work independently and meet deadlines • Professional, dependable, and trustworthy • Payroll and year-end experience is an asset To apply: Please submit your resume and a brief introduction outlining your bookkeeping experience.

title: Maintenance Technician (Ottawa and Surrounding Areas)
description: ## JOIN OUR TEAM! At Couche-Tard/Circle K, our mission is simple: to make our customer's lives a little easier everyday. You may have already stopped for coffee, refueling your car, or eating something on the go. Then, you know what Couche-Tard/Circle K is. We have grown into a successful global company with over 16,000 stores in 29 countries, serving almost 9 million customers every day. In total, more than 150,000 people work in our stores and offices. We make journeys easier by offering fast and friendly service. We care about our people and our communities, and we look for ways to uplift people first. Wherever your journey's going, we can help you get there.?? Are you ready to grow your career? Let's grow together! ## ## Maintenance Technician Department: Facilities and Construction Location: Ottawa and Surrounding Areas, ON Type of Employment: Permanent, Full Time (37.5 hours) Reason for Posting: Existing Vacancy (5 positions) Salary: $50,000 - $60,000 CAD per year ## THE ROLE We are currently hiring for a Maintenance Technician to join our Central Canada Maintenance Team. Reporting to the Maintenance Manager the Maintenance Technician will maintain store operations. In this role you will be responsible for conducting preventative maintenance primarily on Frozen Beverage Equipment, repairing Convenience Store equipment and general maintenance work in stores. ## WHAT YOU'LL DO Excited to embark on a journey with us? Here's a breakdown of the key responsibilities in this role: • (Primary daily function) Perform Preventative Maintenance on Frozen Beverage units. • Maintains equipment by troubleshooting, repairing, cleaning, and performing preventative maintenance. • Maintains facilities by performing light electrical, plumbing, carpentry, roofing, cleaning, lighting work. • Maintains continuity among work teams by documenting and communicating actions, irregularities, and continuing needs. • Ensures preventative repairs are performed cost effectively by examining records, reports operating practices and other documentation. • Participate in training classes for existing and new equipment. • Ensures maintenance operations by initiating, coordinating, and enforcing program, operation policies and procedures. • Contributes to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed. • Maintain professional and technical knowledge by attending educational workshops; reading professional publications; establishing personal networks; participating in professional societies. • Maintains safe and healthy work environment by abiding to safety policies and procedures; ensuring compliance with federal, state and local requirements. • Majority of time will be spent in the field • May require some travel including overnight stay ## Physical Demands: • Ability to crouch, crawl, push, pull, bend, stoop and/or reach. • Ability to carry, erect and climb ladders. • Ability to lift as much as 80 pounds. ## WHY YOU SHOULD WORK HERE: At Couche-Tard/Circle K, we believe that our team members are the heart and soul of our business. When you join us, you're not just getting a job - you're becoming part of a vibrant community where your talents are valued, your growth is nurtured, and your contributions make a real difference. Here's why you'll love working with us: ## Benefits package: • Group Insurance Program: Stay healthy and happy! Our plan provides you with the flexibility to choose coverage that best meets your needs and add optional insurance (health and dental care, long-term disability, life insurance, health spending account) • Pension Plan: Plan for your future and retire with peace of mind with our pension plan, helping you build a secure financial future. • Share Purchase Plan: Invest in your future and share in our success with our employee stock purchase plan, allowing you to become a shareholder of Couche-Tard/Circle K. • Paid Time Off: Recharge and rejuvenate with paid time off, including vacation days, sick days, and personal days to help you maintain a healthy work-life balance. ## Additional Perks: • Training and Development: Grow your skills and advance your career with access to ongoing training and development opportunities, including workshops, seminars, and online courses. • Recognition and Rewards: We celebrate our team's achievements and milestones with a range of recognition programs, rewards, and incentives to show our appreciation for your hard work and dedication. • Mentorship Program: Take your career to new heights with our mentorship program, where seasoned professionals provide guidance, support, and valuable insights to help you reach your full potential. • Scholarship Program: Invest in your education and future success with our scholarship program, available not only to our employees but also to their children. We're committed to supporting your lifelong learning journey and empowering you to achieve your academic and career goals. INTERESTED? You are only a few clicks away from joining an exceptional company! Visit our careers page at https://workwithus.circlek.com/ca/en to submit your application. We can't wait to hear from you! Circle K values diversity in the workplace and encourages applications from the following designated groups: women, aboriginal peoples, persons with disabilities and members of visible minorities. We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Accommodations are available on request in all aspects of the selection process. We use artificial intelligence (AI) to match job profiles with job requirements as part of our recruitment process. This position reflects an open vacancy. We thank all candidates for their interest in this position. Please note that only selected candidates will be contacted for further steps in the hiring process. ## WHAT YOU'LL NEED We want you to join our team! Here's what we're looking for: ## Education: • High school diploma or GED preferred. ## Experience: • 3-5 years' experience in the maintenance field. • 1-2 years' experience in C-store Preventative Maintenance, food service repairs, plumbing or HVAC/refrigeration preferred. ## Knowledge and skills: • Able to work in a fast-paced environment with multiple changing priorities and ability to work independently. • Must have a valid Ontario driver's license, clean driving record and be insurable as a driver. • Highly organized and work well under pressure/deadlines with the ability to multi-task.

title: UX Research and Design Student
description: The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We leverage diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you! ## Job Description We're looking for students to join our team through both Student and Co-op opportunities! As a UX Research and Design Student, you will support user-centred design activities that contribute to the development and improvement of digital products and services at the House of Commons. Working as part of a collaborative team in an Agile environment, you will have the opportunity to participate in user research, help plan and conduct usability testing, collect and analyze user feedback, and contribute to interface design and usability validation. You will also support the development of wireframes and interactive prototypes, apply accessibility and visual design principles, and contribute to UX standards and guidelines. This role offers hands-on experience working with stakeholders and users while applying UX research and design practices to real-world digital initiatives that support the work of Parliament. We are looking for students who have knowledge of, and some experience with, one or more of the following: • User research methodologies and approaches; • Collecting and analyzing user data and feedback; • Planning and preparing user research studies; • Facilitating or supporting usability testing; • User-centred interface design processes; • Visual design principles; • Information architecture and interaction design; • Developing wireframes; • Developing interactive prototypes for usability testing; • Applying UX research findings and user feedback to design solutions; • Designing digital experiences with accessibility in mind. Experience may have been gained through academic projects, work experience, volunteer activities, personal projects or other relevant experiences. ## Top Reasons to Join the House of Commons Administration : • Inclusive work environment: Be part of a team that values diversity and fosters inclusivity. • Competitive compensation: Earn a competitive hourly salary that supports your education. • Real-world application: Gain hands-on experience by applying classroom knowledge to real-world scenarios. • Skill enhancement and growth: Build valuable skills and grow professionally with expert guidance. • Career development: Access numerous opportunities for learning and career advancement after graduation. ## Qualifications ## Education?: • Current enrollment as a full-time student at an accredited post-secondary institution and registration in a co-op program. ## Additional Information We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free recruitment and selection process. If you have an accommodation request, require material in an accessible format, or need additional support with the application process, please contact Recruitment and Selection Services at?HOCCareers-CarrieresCDC@parl.gc.ca. Eligibility criteria: • Minimum age of 16 • Canadian citizenship, permanent residency or a valid study permit (for international students) The Co-op position is located in Ottawa, Ontario and you will be required to work on-site. While we appreciate all applications, only those selected for further consideration will receive a response due to the volume of submissions.? If you're not enrolled in a co-op program but are seeking student employment opportunities, we encourage you to visit our?website?and apply to the 'Student Employment Program'. Learn more about us! Visit?Ourcommons.ca. To learn about our hiring process, visit?Eligibility and Selection. L'Administration de la Chambre des communes fournit aux députés et à leur personnel des services exceptionnels afin d'appuyer la démocratie parlementaire. Notre main-d'œuvre talentueuse et dévouée est au cœur de notre succès. Nous valorisons la diversité sous toutes ses formes et nous reconnaissons que chacun peut apporter une contribution et a le potentiel de s'épanouir. Si vous rêvez de vous joindre à une organisation assez petite pour que l'on vous remarque, mais assez grande pour vous offrir une belle carrière, nous voulons vous connaître ! ## Description du poste Nous cherchons des étudiant·e·s pour se joindre à notre équipe dans le cadre de possibilités d'emploi étudiant et de stages coop! En tant qu'étudiant·e en recherche et conception UX, vous appuierez des activités de conception centrée sur les utilisateur·rice·s qui contribuent au développement et à l'amélioration des produits et services numériques de la Chambre des communes. En travaillant au sein d'une équipe collaborative dans un environnement Agile, vous aurez l'occasion de participer à la recherche auprès des utilisateur·rice·s, d'aider à planifier et à réaliser des tests d'utilisabilité, de recueillir et d'analyser les commentaires des utilisateur·rice·s, et de contribuer à la conception d'interfaces et à la validation de leur utilisabilité. Vous contribuerez également au développement de maquettes fonctionnelles et de prototypes interactifs, à l'application des principes d'accessibilité et de conception visuelle, ainsi qu'aux normes et lignes directrices en matière d'expérience utilisateur (UX). Ce rôle offre une expérience pratique de collaboration avec les parties prenantes et les utilisateur·rice·s, tout en permettant d'appliquer des pratiques de recherche et de conception UX à des initiatives numériques concrètes qui soutiennent les travaux du Parlement. Nous recherchons des étudiant·e·s qui possèdent des connaissances et une certaine expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : • Méthodologies et approches de recherche auprès des utilisateur·rice·s; • Collecte et analyse de données et de commentaires des utilisateur·rice·s; • Planification et préparation d'études de recherche auprès des utilisateur·rice·s; • Animation ou soutien de tests d'utilisabilité; • Processus de conception d'interfaces centrée sur les utilisateur·rice·s; • Principes de conception visuelle; • Architecture de l'information et conception d'interactions; • Développement de maquettes fonctionnelles; • Développement de prototypes interactifs aux fins de tests d'utilisabilité; • Application des résultats de la recherche UX et des commentaires des utilisateur·rice·s aux solutions de conception; • Conception d'expériences numériques tenant compte de l'accessibilité. L'expérience peut avoir été acquise dans le cadre de projets universitaires, d'une expérience de travail, d'activités bénévoles, de projets personnels ou d'autres expériences pertinentes. Principales raisons de se joindre à l'Administration de la Chambre des communes : • Environnement de travail inclusif : Faites partie d'une équipe qui valorise la diversité et favorise l'inclusion. • Rémunération compétitive : Gagnez un salaire horaire concurrentiel qui vous permet de poursuivre vos études. • Application dans le monde réel : Acquérir une expérience pratique en appliquant les connaissances acquises en classe à des scénarios réels. • Amélioration et développement des compétences : Développez des compétences précieuses et évoluez professionnellement grâce aux conseils d'un expert. • Développement de carrière : Accédez à de nombreuses possibilités d'apprentissage et d'évolution de carrière après l'obtention de votre diplôme. ## Qualifications ## Éducation : • Être actuellement inscrit·e à temps plein dans un établissement d'enseignement postsecondaire agréé et être inscrit·e à un programme coop. ## Informations supplémentaires Nous nous engageons à créer un milieu de travail inclusif, notamment en adoptant un processus de recrutement et de sélection sans obstacle. Si vous avez une demande d'adaptation, avez besoin de matériel dans un format accessible, ou d'un soutien supplémentaire dans le cadre du processus de candidature, veuillez communiquer avec l'équipe des Services de recrutement et de sélection à l'adresse HOCCareers-CarrieresCDC@parl.gc.ca. Critères d'éligibilité : • Âge minimum de 16 ans • Citoyenneté canadienne, résidence permanente ou permis d'études valide (pour les étudiant?e?s étranger?ère?s) Le poste coop est situé à Ottawa, en Ontario, et vous devrez travailler sur place. title: Cataloguing Agent
description: ## ME-03 - $58,980 to $70,901 per year ## Temporary full-time position (37.5 hours per week) for approximately one year. ## Work Location : Natural Heritage Campus (NHC) - Gatineau, QC ## Selection process number: 2090-CMN-26-OC-044 ## Your place at the Museum We value diversity and believe we benefit from working in a place where everyone feels included and where the unique qualities and strengths inherent in a diverse workforce are combined. We welcome applications from persons who may identify as a member of one or more other equity seeking groups (for e.g. women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+, religious or cultural minority). You have a place at the Museum! ## About the position Under the direction of the Head, Library, Archives and Special Collections, catalogues the library documents (mainly monographs and periodicals), using the Integrated Library System (LIS) V-Smart-Air and a variety of library cataloguing tools; assist with the organisation and description of the cataloguing backlog; serve as a library assistant. ## Working at the museum means: • Contributing to an engaging mission as well as exciting projects and challenges • An inclusive, friendly and safe work environment • A competitive salary established by collective agreements • Access to federal public service group insurance and pension plans ## Interested? APPLY! The Canadian Museum of Nature is committed to inclusive and barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If you are invited to participate in the selection process, we encourage you to advise us of any accommodation you may require. This information will be treated as confidential. The Statement of Qualifications, providing greater detail about the skills, knowledge and aptitudes needed for this role, can be obtained by contacting the Museum at competition@nature.ca. All candidates must submit a cover letter and curriculum vitae outlining how their experience and training meet the requirements listed above. Send your application by filling in the form on the Museum's Careers page where you can upload your cover letter, curriculum vitae and any other required documents. ## CLOSING DATE : October 6th, 2026 ## Eligibility criteria This position is open to all Employees of the Canadian Museum of Nature and any members of the public who meet the qualifications below. Candidates must be legally entitled to work in Canada. ## Education and training: Completion of a post-secondary education in the field of Library sciences. ## Language requirements: English or French Bilingualism is considered an asset. ## Experience: • A minimum of 2 years of recent professional experience in delivering MARC 21 standard cataloguing services in an automated library environment. • A minimum of 2 years of recent professional experience in working with library cataloguing tools e.g. RDA, AARC2, Z39.50 protocol, Web classification, Library of Congress Subject Heading, RVM, etc. • A minimum of 2 years of professional experience in original and derived cataloguing of a broad range of publication types (ex.: monographs, periodicals, reports, foreign language publications, electronic resources, etc.) • Experience in making recommendations for improving workflows and processes in response to library needs and priorities • Recent experience in working with an online library system. ## The following experiences are considered assets: • Experience cataloguing in a scientific library • Experience with V-SMART Air library system.

title: Language Assistant
employer: Official Languages Programs/ Programme de langues officielles
description: The Odyssey Language Assistant Program (established in 1973, to promote Canada's two official languages and the cultures they convey) is a paid, professional work experience that involves travelling to Quebec or New Brunswick to work with students for nine months. Earn $30 an hour while gaining valuable work experience in a classroom setting. Working under teacher supervision, you will plan and lead activities on a daily basis to motivate students to learn more about the target language. You will share your culture and the unique linguistic features of your home region through art, music, stories, local expressions, and humour. Your work will consist mostly of: • preparing and executing activities that focus on language (aural comprehension and oral expression); • developing activities that reflect everyday communication opportunities in order to help students improve their English-language skills in real-life situations; • drawing from your own interests and those of the students, this is an opportunity to use your talents and passions to help someone build skills in English, and to have fun doing it; • examples include starting a debate, playing a trivia game, putting on a play, and teaching a dance or a new sport; and The language assistant does not replace the teacher. The tasks of a language assistant may include the following: • encouraging students to participate in oral communication activities; • preparing classroom activities that focus on learning about language and culture; • leading small groups of two to 10 students; • motivating students to learn English; • encouraging students to appreciate and explore your culture and their own in a respectful and creative way through language; • participating in evening and weekend cultural activities; • meeting with school staff upon request. ## Benefits: • Paid leave • Professional training and development program • Reimbursement for kilometers travelled • Reimbursement of training and development activities • Social activities organized by the company • Travel • Competitive salary • Free parking • Paid sick leave • Supplies • Telework • Vacation There is no age limit for undertaking an Odyssey. To qualify, you must meet all of the following criteria: • have excellent English-language skills, both oral and written. English must be your first language, OR your proficiency in English must be as strong as if it were your first language; • be either a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident (those studying in Canada on a student visa are not eligible); • have completed one of the following within the last 10 years: • For studies outside Quebec in Canada - at least one full year of postsecondary studies, in either college or university; • For studies in Quebec - two years of college-level studies or one full year of university; • For studies outside Canada - at least one full year of postsecondary studies, in either college or university. You will also need to submit a formal assessment of your academic credentials. You do not need any French-language skills to apply and participate in the program. However, you will be placed in francophone communities, where French is the first language, so basic speaking skills in French will greatly enhance your experience. The Council of Ministers of Education, Canada (CMEC) thanks all candidates for their interest in Odyssey. Decisions regarding eligibility for participation in the program are made by the relevant provincial and territorial ministries/departments responsible for education or postsecondary education and are also subject to the participating educational institutions' policies, practices, and regulations. A candidate may be declared ineligible for participation in the program at any time, including but without limitation, if the candidate • has been previously dismissed from the program for any reason, • does not or ceases to meet the eligibility criteria for or the conditions for participation in the program, • does not meet any requirement or condition of the relevant provincial and territorial ministries/departments responsible for education or postsecondary education or of the participating educational institutions' policies, practices, and regulations.

title: Canadian Coast Guard Inshore Rescue Boat (IRB) student program (Summer 2026)
description: ## Inshore Rescue Boat (IRB) Program - Canadian Coast Guard Each summer, the Canadian Coast Guard offers students a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience while making a real difference. Through the Inshore Rescue Boat (IRB) Program, students provide on-water search and rescue services and work closely with local partners to help mariners in need. Applications for Summer 2027 are now open! The deadline to apply is November 2, 2026. Who we're looking for: We're seeking students who hold the following certifications: • Standard First Aid with CPR-C and AED • Pleasure Craft Operator Card (or equivalent) • Restricted Radio Operator Certificate - Maritime (ROC-M) with VHF DSC endorsement • A valid, unrestricted Canadian driver's licence (Note: graduated licences with restrictions are not accepted) Join a Virtual Info Session Want to learn more? We're hosting online information sessions about the IRB Program: • English session: Tuesday, September 29, 2026 @7:00 EST • French session: Thursday, October 1, 2026 @ 7:00 pm EST Space is limited-register early to secure your spot! __________________________________________________________________________________________________ ## ## Canadian Coast Guard Inshore Rescue Boat (IRB) student program (Summer 2027) Federal Student Work Experience Program Closing date: November 2, 2026 - 23:59, Pacific Standard Time ## National Defence / Canadian Coast Guard ## Location Dartmouth (Nova Scotia), Québec (Québec), Sarnia (Ontario), St. John's (Newfoundland and Labrador), Victoria (British Columbia) ## Job type Full-time ## Salary $20.16 - Crew Member / $26.46 - Coxswain ## Number of jobs The IRB student program employs approximately 100 Crew Members & 42 Coxswains nationally ## Contact information DFO.CCGStudentRecruitmentProgram-ProgrammeDeRecrutementGCC.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca Apply now Find out about rates of pay FSWEP eligibility criteria Gear Up, Save Lives, Make a Difference. Apply to be a crew member of the Inshore Rescue Boat (IRB) student program. ## What you will gain • training in search and rescue operations; • rewarding real-world experience in delivering on-water search and rescue; • experience working with local agencies during rescues and other incidents; • opportunities for professional growth and leadership roles; • development of professional networks, including with other students; • access to many exciting and rewarding career opportunities with the Canadian Coast Guard (CCG). ## What you will do Search and Rescue operations can occur at any time of the day or night, during all types of weather and sea conditions. As part of a crew, you have the serious responsibility of responding to mariners in distress or need of assistance, including but not limited to: • vessels that are disabled, aground, capsized, broken down, lost in the fog, taking on water; • persons overboard; • medical emergencies. At minimum, each IRB crew consists of one (1) Coxswain and two (2) crew members. ## When will you work? • Summer contract period will range from the end of April 2027 to early September 2027 (may vary by location and operational needs). • Crews operate on a rotating schedule of 14 consecutive days of work followed by 14 days of rest. During your 14 days of work, you will live and work with your crew. Regional differences may apply. • To maintain pay continuity throughout the contract period, payment is averaged over both days of work and days of rest. • Lodging and a shared meal budget will be provided during your scheduled work periods. CCG does not provide living arrangements or meals during off-duty periods. ## Where will you work? The Canadian Coast Guard's Inshore Rescue Boat Service operates 25 stations across Canada. During your application, you will be asked to indicate your preferred region for employment. Due to operational requirements, please note that your training location as well as your assigned location for search and rescue operations may differ from your initial preference. Geographic flexibility is therefore required for the entire duration of the process and the employment period. To learn more about station locations, please visit the Inshore Rescue Boat station locations page. ## Atlantic Region Stations (Dartmouth and St. John's) • Maritimes: the stations are located in Saint John (NB), Shediac (NB), Halifax (NS), Mahone Bay (NS), Pictou (NS) and Charlottetown (PE). • Newfoundland & Labrador (NL): the stations are located in Conception Bay South, Terra Nova National Park, and Lewisporte. ## Central Region Stations (Québec and Sarnia) • Great Lakes (ON): the stations are located on Gereaux Island, in Twelve Mile Bay, in Corunna, St. Williams, on Hill Island, and in Mitchell's Bay. • St. Lawrence (QC): the stations are located in Saint-Anicet, Vaudreuil, Beaconsfield, Longueuil, Sorel, and Trois-Rivières. ## Western Region Stations (Victoria) • Victoria (BC): the stations are located in Nootka Sound, Sointula, Cortes and Kelsey Bay. ## ## What we are looking for We are looking for full-time post-secondary students who: • are reliable, calm, and able to make safe and sound decisions in a high stress environment; • are hardworking and motivated people who are eager, willing to learn, and ready to work in difficult conditions; • are fluent in French to work in the province of Québec and fluent in English to work in all other regions; • have general knowledge of marine safety. ## Are you eligible? To be eligible for the IRB student program, you must meet and be able to provide proof of the following requirements: • be registered as a full-time student in a post-secondary accredited academic institution, this includes persons with disabilities considered to have full-time status by their academic institution; • meet the minimum age requirement to be employed in the province or territory of work; • be returning to full-time studies in the next academic term, in Fall 2027 session. Preference will be given to candidates with Canadian citizenship or permanent resident status over non?Canadians who are eligible to work in Canada. See the Directive on Student Employment for more information on the Government of Canada's requirements for student employment. For more information on eligibility, please visit Federal Student Work Experience Program (FSWEP). All information collected during the selection process, including behaviour and communication, from the time of application to the end of the process, may be used to assess candidates and make hiring decisions. ## Conditions of employment You must meet and maintain the following conditions during employment: • Applicants are responsible for obtaining the following: • • a valid Standard First Aid certification with CPR-C/AED certification, or accepted equivalent certification; • a valid Pleasure Craft Operator Card or accepted certificate of equivalency; • a valid Restricted Radio Operator Certificate - Maritime (ROC-M) with VHF Digital Selective Calling (DSC) endorsement; • a valid unrestricted driver's license* that allows you to drive a motor vehicle in Canada. *Note: A valid driver's licence is a full driver's licence. This does not include a driver's licence with restrictions as part of any provincial graduated licencing. You will be asked to present an original, unrestricted driver's licence. • If your application is selected, CCG will coordinate the following: • successfully complete the National IRB marine knowledge exam and interview; • successfully complete the IRB Program assessment; • obtain and maintain a reliability security status; Learn about the security screening process. • complete and meet the standards of a Health Canada Medical exam which includes a: • hearing test • physical examination • colour-vision examination; • successfully complete the paid training course (approximately 16 days) on water and in the classroom, including written and practical examinations, that certifies candidates in: • Marine Advanced First Aid (MAFA) or Advanced Medical First Responder (AMFR) (may vary depending on training location) • CCG Small Craft Training Basic Course • Marine Emergency Duties - Small non-pleasure domestic vessel basic safety (SDV-BS) • Small Vessel Operator Proficiency (SVOP) training • CCG Rigid Hull Inflatable Operator Training (RHIOT) course (may vary depending on training location) • Applicants must also: • Maintain strict adherence to the Department of National Defence and Canadian Forces Code of Values and Ethics, Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector, Directive on Conflict of Interest, and Defence Administrative Orders and Directives (DAOD) 7021-1, Conflict of Interest. • work full-time hours and various shifts, including weekends and holidays; • work overtime as required; • be redeployed to another rescue station during employment if necessary, based on operational needs. • wear and maintain the provided CCG uniform to CCG uniform standards; • use and maintain all personal protective equipment when in the operational field as per CCG policies and directives; • adhere to the IRB Operational Standing Orders and Standard Operating Procedures. ## Additional information • The Canadian Coast Guard is a special operating agency within the Department of National Defence. Effective September 1, 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard has transferred from the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) to the Department of National Defence (DND) by Order-in-Council. • It is your responsibility to verify your email, including monitoring your junk/spam folders, for new communication regarding this selection process, and to inform us of any change of address, phone number and email address by contacting DFO.CCGStudentRecruitmentProgram-ProgrammeDeRecrutementGCC.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca. • If you are not notified by the end of January 2027, you will not be considered for summer 2027 positions; we encourage you to re-apply next year if you still meet the eligibility requirements. • A pool of qualified candidates will be established from this selection process, but not all applicants will be hired. • Candidates can expect to receive communications within 1 week of the closing date. • Information about lodging and meals during training will be provided by regional Coast Guard staff. No employment is granted until all parts of the training have been successfully completed ## Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion The Department of National Defence is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive team that reflects Canada's population. To achieve a representative workforce, selection may be based on qualified candidates self-declaring as belonging to one or more of the designated groups: Indigenous Peoples, members of visible minorities, persons with disabilities, and women. title: HubSpot Web and Email Production Specialist
description: Take the brief, build the thing, ship it clean. Remote (Canada-wide, Ottawa preferred) · 4-day work week · Reports to the VP of Marketing ## Background Okay, so here's the deal; LemonadeLXP is scaling fast, and marketing is scaling with it. HubSpot is our campaign engine, HockeyStack tells us what's actually working, and we've got more campaigns in the pipe than we have hands to build them. That's where you come in. We need someone who can take a campaign brief and use that to generate copy, supporting images and designs, and turn it all into a live, tested, on-brand digital experience. Every single time. Got it. But what's LemonadeLXP? We're flat out the best learning and knowledge platform in the world. What the hell does that mean, you ask? Coles Notes: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=exsGlnr_Tpl Deep Dive: www.lemonadelxp.com If you'd rather build the thing than sit in a meeting about building the thing, we need to talk! ## The Sitch We are looking for a hands-on HubSpot Email & Web Production Specialist to turn campaign briefs copy, and creative concepts into polished digital experiences. You will build and publish responsive emails, landing pages, forms, pop-ups, and blog posts in HubSpot. You will use HTML and CSS to adapt templates, solve layout problems, and accurately translate approved designs into finished digital marketing assets. You will work closely with our marketing leader, demand gen lead, designer, and Sales Operations team. When additional creative is needed, you will help prepare clear design briefs, work with our designer, and use approved AI tools to generate or adapt supporting assets. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career digital producer who enjoys building things, has strong attention to detail, and wants to deepen their HubSpot, email, and web-production skills. ## The Work • Build, test, and publish marketing emails, landing pages, forms, pop-ups, and blog posts in HubSpot. • Translate approved designs into responsive, on-brand implementations using HubSpot's editors, templates, HTML, and CSS. • Format and stage campaign content supplied by our marketing and content teams. • Prepare digital assets by resizing, cropping, compressing, and optimizing images for email and web use. • Create clear briefs for our designer or use approved AI tools when additional campaign assets are required. • Perform thorough pre-launch quality assurance across desktop and mobile, including links, personalization, layout, metadata, forms, and tracking. • Configure campaign associations, tracking URLs, lists, and straightforward workflows based on documented campaign requirements. • Maintain reusable templates, modules, asset libraries, naming conventions, and production checklists. • Implement approved A/B tests and document the results. • Monitor basic email, page, and form performance and produce routine campaign reports. • Identify technical or production issues and work with the appropriate team member to resolve them. ## The Fit You're the ideal candidate for this gig if you can demonstrate: • Practical HTML and CSS skills, including an understanding of responsive layouts. • Strong visual judgment and attention to typography, spacing, alignment, and brand consistency. • A methodical approach to testing and quality assurance. • The ability to work from a brief and turn requirements into a finished digital asset. • The judgment to recognize unclear requirements and ask good questions before building. • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple production assignments. • Comfort learning unfamiliar software and troubleshooting technical problems. • Clear written and verbal communication skills. • An interest in email marketing, web production, automation, and digital customer experiences. We care more about demonstrated ability than a specific number of years in the industry. Relevant work may come from employment, internships, freelance assignments, school projects, volunteer work, or personal projects. ## The Proof Please provide a résumé and two or three examples of relevant work. These could include emails, landing pages, websites, templates, or other digital projects that demonstrate your HTML/CSS skills, visual attention to detail, or production process. We welcome early-career applicants and do not expect every candidate to have worked in HubSpot. If you can demonstrate strong fundamentals, careful execution, and an ability to learn, we would like to hear from you. ## The Close You'll have us at hello if you can show us: • Experience with HubSpot Marketing Hub or another email marketing, CMS, or marketing automation platform. • Experience building or editing HTML emails. • Familiarity with HubSpot Design Tools or HubL. • Experience with Figma, Canva, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Express, or similar creative tools. • Experience using generative AI tools to develop or adapt marketing assets. • Basic knowledge of email accessibility, deliverability, personalization, and testing. • Familiarity with SEO fundamentals, analytics, campaign tracking, or A/B testing. • Experience working in B2B SaaS, EdTech, microlearning, or financial services. • A HubSpot Academy certification.

As a personal care attendant with Whimble, you will provide one-on-one, person-centred support to individuals with physical, developmental, and/or mental health disabilities in their daily lives and in the community. ## Key Responsibilities • Provide direct, hands-on support to individuals with physical, developmental, and/or mental health disabilities, including assistance with daily living activities such as personal care, hygiene, feeding. • Work independently in client homes and community settings, using sound judgment and initiative without constant supervision. • Support clients in building life skills, independence, communication, and social connections. • Safely accompany and support clients in the community, including outings, appointments, errands, recreational activities, and social events. • Feel confident navigating public spaces, transit, and new environments alongside clients. • Proactively identify client needs, anticipate challenges, and respond calmly and effectively. • Implement individualized support plans and behaviour support strategies with consistency and care. • Build positive, respectful relationships with clients and their families. • Take ownership of schedules, responsibilities, and client experiences while remaining reliable and accountable. • Other duties as required to support client wellbeing. ## Ideal Candidate This role is best suited for someone who is highly self-motivated, proactive, and comfortable working independently. Whimble attendants are required to take initiative, apply common sense, and support clients confidently without on-site supervision. • Highly self-motivated and proactive. • Comfortable working independently and making decisions in real time. • Confident supporting clients in public and community settings. • Reliable, organized, and accountable. • Calm, adaptable, and solution-oriented. • Compassionate, respectful, and person-centred. • Strong situational awareness and sound judgment. ## Why Join Us • Flexible scheduling and diverse experiences across the community. • Meaningful work that supports autonomy, independence, and community inclusion. • A role that values initiative, trust, and self-direction. ## Qualifications • Experience supporting individuals with physical, developmental, and/or mental health disabilities, including personal care routines (bathing, bowel and bladder care) involving mechanical lifts, such as Hoyer lifts, ceiling lifts, and other patient lift & transfer equipment. • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including attentiveness to verbal and non-verbal cues, empathy, patience, a sense of humour, and a positive attitude. • Ability to work independently with strong time management, initiative, accountability, and real-time problem-solving skills. • Comfortable supporting clients in the community, adapting to changing environments, and taking direction from clients during tasks. • Familiarity with conflict resolution and de-escalation techniques. • Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including mornings, evenings, and weekends, and willingness to pick up shifts on short notice. • Good working knowledge of spoken and written English. • Smartphone with data plan. • Proof of full COVID-19 vaccination (minimum 3 doses). • A recent negative 1-Step TST or a negative 2-Step TST. • Proof of valid CPR + First Aid training. • Clear vulnerable sector police check performed within the last 6 months. • Adequate liability insurance coverage for performing standard tasks expected of a personal care attendant. • Eagerness to try something new and help shape an innovative tech startup. • Diploma or education in Developmental Services Worker (DSW), or Personal Support Worker (PSW) with experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities. • Access to a reliable vehicle and valid driver's license is considered a strong asset. • Willingness to transport clients as needed (where applicable). ## Compensation Services provided through Whimble are compensated at $30/hour. Hours worked will be paid out weekly upon receipt of an invoice. ## Application Process Please submit: • A brief cover letter explaining why you think you'd be a good fit. • If your application proceeds past the interview stage, you will need to provide: • 2 professional references from individuals to whom you have directly provided personal care assistance. • Photo of government-issued photo ID. • Valid CPR and First Aid training. • Proof of liability insurance coverage (include scan/photo of your policy that clearly shows your name, policy #, insurer name, validity date, and type of coverage). • Recent Level 3 Vulnerable Sector Check (must be completed within last 6 months). • Proof of COVID-19 vaccination (min. of 3 doses). • Recent 1- or 2-step TBT. • Photo and a couple sentences about yourself for your Attendant profile that we send to clients before you arrive. • Emergency Contact Info (name, phone #, email and relation to you). Please note: by submitting an application to Whimble Care Inc, you are confirming that you are legally eligible to work in Canada. title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (pregnancy/family leave replacement one year)
description: ## ORCC Job Posting Psychotherapist/Counsellor (this is a one-year pregnancy/family leave replacement with possibility of renewal) Organization: Ottawa Rape Crisis Centre (ORCC) Location: Ottawa, Ontario (Hybrid: In-person & Virtual) Hours: Full-Time (37.5 hours per week) Reports to: Management Program: Counselling Services ## About ORCC The Ottawa Rape Crisis Centre (ORCC) is a registered charity founded in 1974. We provide individual and group counselling, crisis support, service navigation, psychoeducation, and advocacy to support survivors and advance systemic change. Our work is grounded in survivor-centred, trauma-informed, and anti-oppressive principles. ## The Opportunity ORCC is seeking a skilled, compassionate, and values-aligned Psychotherapist / Counsellor to provide direct counselling and psychotherapy services to individuals aged 16 and older who have experienced sexual and/or gender-based violence. The Psychotherapist / Counsellor will provide the controlled act of psychotherapy within ORCC?s counselling program, ensuring consistent, ethical, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive care. This role is central to the reliable delivery of funded counselling services and contributes to ORCC?s mandate of supporting survivors through accessible, survivor-centred services. We are seeking a reflective and collaborative clinician who is committed to equity-informed practice, professional accountability, and working within a team-based service environment. ## Key Responsibilities ## Direct Psychotherapy and Counselling Services • Provide culturally responsive, trauma-informed, evidence-based psychotherapy and counselling to survivors of sexual and/or gender-based violence, aged 16 and older. • Maintain an active caseload in accordance with ORCC clinical policy. • Deliver services in alignment with ORCC clinical guidelines, intake criteria, and service timelines. • Apply therapeutic modalities consistent with organizational standards, professional scope, and client needs. ## Caseload, Scheduling & Service Delivery • Maintain a weekly schedule that prioritizes direct client service delivery in alignment with ORCC clinical policy and organizational needs. • Coordinate client hours, availability, and non-client time with management. • Support consistent and reliable access to counselling services for clients. ## Intake, Treatment Planning & Discharge • Conduct intake assessments and develop individualized treatment plans. • Communicate service timelines clearly with clients. • Engage in ongoing discharge planning throughout the counselling process. • Consult with management regarding session extensions or service adjustments in accordance with ORCC clinical policy. ## Clinical Documentation & Compliance • Maintain timely, complete, and accurate clinical records in ORCC?s electronic client record system. • Ensure documentation meets organizational quality, risk management, privacy, and compliance standards. • Track and report counselling statistics and service data as required. ## Clinical Supervision & Professional Accountability • Participate in regularly scheduled clinical supervision. • Integrate supervisory feedback into clinical practice. • Practice within the scope of professional competence and applicable regulatory requirements, including CRPO and/or OCSWSSW standards. ## Groups, Workshops & Program Activities • Facilitate group counselling or psychoeducational workshops as assigned or approved by management. • Contribute to counselling program activities that align with ORCC?s mandate and service priorities. ## Referrals & Community Coordination • Provide referrals to external services for clients whose needs fall outside the scope of ORCC services. • Collaborate with community partners within assigned responsibilities. • Contribute to systems navigation through referral, coordination, and consultation. • Work collaboratively with designated ORCC roles responsible for primary advocacy and related support. ## Team Collaboration • Participate in staff meetings, team meetings, supervision, and required organizational activities. • Contribute constructively to ORCC?s workplace culture through respectful collaboration, shared problem-solving, and reflective practice. • Support an organizational environment grounded in equity, accountability, and staff wellbeing. ## Qualifications • Master?s degree in Counselling, Social Work, Psychotherapy, or a related field. • Current registration and member in good standing with a relevant regulatory college, such as CRPO or OCSWSSW, and authorized to practice the controlled act of psychotherapy. • Minimum of two years of relevant clinical counselling/psychotherapy experience preferred; equivalent combinations of clinical training, supervised practice, and relevant experience will be considered. • Clinical training and/or demonstrated experience in evidence-based trauma-focused therapies (e.g., EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy [CPT], Prolonged Exposure [PE], or related approaches) is considered an asset. • Experience assessing and responding to complex trauma presentation, co-occurring mental health concerns, and elevated clinical risk is an asset. • Experience facilitating therapeutic groups and/or psychoeducational programming is an asset. • Experience working with survivors of sexual and/or gender-based violence is an asset. • Experience supporting marginalized and underserved communities is an asset. ## Skills & Competencies • Strong clinical judgment and ethical decision-making skills. • Demonstrated ability to provide trauma-informed, survivor-centred counselling. • Commitment to anti-oppressive, culturally responsive, and equity-informed practice. • Ability to develop treatment plans and support clients through structured service timelines. • Strong documentation, organization, and time-management skills. • Ability to manage an active caseload while maintaining professional boundaries and self-reflective practice. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment. • Familiarity with risk management, confidentiality, privacy, and professional regulatory obligations. • Knowledge of the impacts of sexual and gender-based violence, including the intersections of trauma, power, identity, systemic oppression, and barriers to help-seeking, is an asset. • Excellent written and verbal English; additional languages are an asset. ## Working Conditions • Full-time position, 37.5 hours per week. • Hybrid model with in-person and virtual responsibilities. • Vulnerable sector police record check required. • Participation in clinical supervision and team meetings required. • Ability to work within Ottawa and attend in-person duties as needed. ## Salary & Benefits • Salary Range: $65,000-$80,000, commensurate with experience. • Total Compensation Package: $80,000?$95,000 annually. • Comprehensive benefits package including extended health and dental coverage, generous paid leave, employer RRSP matching, professional licensing coverage, and professional development support. ## How to Apply To apply, or request more information, please send a cover letter and your resume to: Bryn.Davies@orcc.net ORCC is an equal opportunity employer, committed to inclusivity and meeting our obligations under the Ontario Human Rights Code. We welcome applications from candidates from diverse backgrounds. If you require accommodation to participate in this recruitment process, please freely indicate your needs. 1 - 2 years of experience
