title: Residential Support Worker (Relief)
description: POSITION INFORMATION Job Title: Residential Support Worker (Relief) Department: Community Residential Facilities (CRF) Reports To: Team Leader, Residential Services, or designate Classification: A (Subject to the Collective Agreement) Programs and Locations: Crossroads Program: 419 Jones Avenue, Toronto, Ontario Donald G. Evans Residence (DGER): 1669 Eglinton Avenue West, Toronto, Ontario Wage: $22.66 per hour, in accordance with the applicable collective agreement. Hourly premiums are also provided in accordance with the collective agreement. Security Clearance Requirement: The successful candidate must be eligible to obtain and maintain an Enhanced Reliability Status security clearance. The screening process requires verification of the candidate?s identity, employment, education, residence and other relevant history for at least the previous five years. Employment is conditional upon successfully obtaining and maintaining the required security clearance. Hours of Work This position operates within a 24-hour Community Residential Facility (CRF) environment. Relief employees are required to maintain flexibility and availability based on operational requirements. Relief staff may be scheduled to work: Day Shifts , Afternoon Shifts Overnight (Awake) Shifts Weekends Statutory Holidays Emergency call-in shifts & Short-notice replacement shifts Employees may be required to work at both Community Residential Facilities and may be assigned to either location based on operational requirements. Collective Agreement This position is governed by the Collective Agreement between the John Howard Society of Toronto and SEIU Healthcare. POSITION SUMMARY The Residential Support Worker provides residential supervision, client support, crisis intervention, case management assistance, and operational oversight within a federally funded Community Residential Facility operated by the John Howard Society of Toronto. The position supports federally sentenced individuals transitioning into the community under Correctional Service Canada supervision, including those on Day Parole, Full Parole, Statutory Release, Long-Term Supervision Orders, or other forms of community supervision. The role promotes public safety and successful reintegration by supporting residents with release-condition compliance, accountability, pro-social behaviour, risk reduction, and access to community resources. Staff must maintain a structured, safe, and professional environment while responding appropriately to complex mental health, substance use, trauma, behavioural, conflict, and emergency situations. Employees must exercise sound judgment, discretion, confidentiality, cultural competency, and professional boundaries while collaborating with CSC, Parole Officers, community agencies, emergency responders, and other stakeholders. They must comply with all organizational policies, contractual obligations, legal requirements, and ethical standards. PROGRAM OVERVIEW Community Residential Facilities The Crossroads Program and Donald G. Evans Residence are federally funded Community Residential Facilities (halfway houses) operating under contract with Correctional Service Canada. Both programs provide structured accommodation, supervision, programming, and reintegration support to federally sentenced individuals released into the community. The programs promote public safety, accountability, law-abiding behaviour, independent living skills, risk reduction, and successful completion of parole or community supervision. Residents must comply with their release conditions, house rules, case management plans, federal legislation, and CSC requirements. Residential Support Workers help maintain the safety, structure, accountability, and daily operation of the residences while providing guidance, support, and intervention consistent with evidence-based correctional practices. 3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES The Residential Support Worker is responsible for maintaining the safe, secure, and effective operation of a Community Residential Facility while providing professional support, supervision, and intervention to federally supervised individuals residing within the program. Duties include, but are not limited to, the following: A. Resident Supervision & Support The Residential Support Worker is responsible for providing continuous supervision and support to residents while maintaining a structured, safe, and accountable residential environment. Employees shall: ? Provide daily supervision of residents in accordance with organizational policies, Correctional Service Canada contractual requirements, and individualized case management plans. ? Maintain awareness of each resident's release conditions, supervision requirements, offence cycle, criminogenic needs, risk factors, behavioural expectations, and case management objectives. ? Monitor compliance with: o Parole Board of Canada conditions o House rules o Curfews o Sign-in/sign-out procedures o Temporary absences o Employment schedules o Programming attendance o Substance restrictions o Visitor procedures ? Verify resident whereabouts and ensure accountability throughout each shift. ? Monitor resident movement within and outside the residence. ? Observe behavioural changes and identify early indicators of deteriorating mental health, substance use, emotional distress, conflict, or escalating risk. ? Provide supportive interventions while maintaining professional boundaries. ? Encourage residents to demonstrate responsibility, accountability, and pro-social decision-making. ? Promote independent living skills through coaching, encouragement, and structured support. ? Maintain fairness, consistency, and objectivity when enforcing house rules and expectations. ? Build professional helping relationships while maintaining clear ethical and professional boundaries at all times. B. Community Reintegration Support Residential Support Workers assist residents with successfully transitioning from federal custody into the community. Employees shall: ? Promote accountability, positive behaviour, and successful community reintegration. ? Help residents establish healthy routines and achieve goals identified in their Correctional Plans. ? Encourage participation in employment, education, treatment, mental health and cultural programming, community services, and volunteer opportunities. ? Support the development of life skills, financial responsibility, time management, communication, problem-solving, and healthy coping strategies. ? Provide information and referrals to appropriate internal and community resources. ? Recognize individual strengths and barriers while promoting long-term stability, independence, and self-sufficiency. C. Case Management Support Residential Support Workers contribute to case management by documenting relevant observations and supporting interdisciplinary communication. Employees shall: ? Review resident files at the beginning of each shift. ? Remain familiar with residents? case management plans, community strategies, special conditions, risk factors, behavioural concerns, medical alerts, mental health needs, and relevant institutional history. ? Observe and accurately document resident progress and behavioural changes. ? Report significant information to Case Managers, Team Leaders, and Parole Officers, as directed. ? Participate in multidisciplinary discussions when requested. ? Encourage attendance at required appointments and correctional programming. ? Assist with appointment and transportation coordination, where applicable. D. House Operations & Residential Monitoring Residential Support Workers maintain the safety, security, cleanliness, and overall operation of the residence throughout each shift. Employees shall: ? Complete scheduled house, curfew, wellness, resident-count, room, building, perimeter, fire-safety, kitchen, common-area, office-security, and equipment checks. ? Monitor cleanliness and ensure residents follow housekeeping expectations. ? Identify safety hazards and promptly report maintenance concerns. ? Secure confidential information and ensure all entrances and exits remain secure. ? Monitor visitors and remain aware of everyone present in the residence. E. Safety, Security & Risk Management Residential Support Workers promote public safety and the safe operation of the residence. Employees shall: ? Maintain situational awareness, identify emerging concerns, and assess changing risk factors throughout each shift. ? Exercise sound judgment when responding to aggression, conflict, substance use, intoxication, mental health deterioration, self-harm concerns, security breaches, and resident absences. ? Conduct authorized room and house searches in accordance with organizational policies and procedures. ? Secure prohibited items and maintain chain-of-custody documentation, where applicable. ? Immediately report safety concerns and follow all applicable lone-worker procedures. ? Protect the safety of residents, visitors, staff, and the public. F. Crisis Intervention & Emergency Response Residential Support Workers must respond calmly, promptly, and professionally to emergencies, including medical incidents, suspected overdoses, fires, behavioural or mental health crises, suicidal ideation, missing residents, violence, security breaches, property damage, criminal activity, natural disasters, and utility failures. Employees shall: ? Conduct immediate risk assessments and use approved verbal de-escalation techniques as the primary intervention. ? Activate emergency procedures and contact emergency services and on-call management as required. ? Coordinate the response until assistance arrives and provide emergency responders with relevant information. ? Maintain resident accountability during evacuations. ? Complete all required documentation before the end of the shift. ? G. Documentation, Reporting & Record Keeping Residential Support Workers must maintain accurate, timely, objective, and professional records that meet organizational, contractual, legal, evidentiary, and Protected B requirements. Documentation may be reviewed or relied upon by CSC, the Parole Board of Canada, law enforcement, legal counsel, auditors, and the courts. Employees shall: ? Complete all required documentation within established timelines and before the end of each shift, unless otherwise directed. ? Accurately record resident interactions, observations, interventions, behavioural changes, and significant events using factual, non-judgmental language. ? Complete required logbook entries, case notes, shift summaries, incident or occurrence reports, database and medication records, emergency and search documentation, maintenance reports, and fire and safety inspection records. ? Follow approved documentation, correction, storage, and Protected B informationhandling procedures. ? Immediately report errors or omissions that could affect resident supervision or public safety. ? Ensure records are complete and capable of withstanding legal, contractual, audit, or investigative review. H. Medication Support Residential Support Workers provide medication support through prompting and observed selfadministration in accordance with organizational policies and applicable legislation. They do not diagnose conditions, prescribe medication, or modify treatment plans. Employees shall: ? Prompt and observe residents taking prescribed medications according to approved schedules. ? Maintain accurate medication records and immediately document and report refusals, missed doses, irregularities, or concerns. ? Secure medications in designated storage areas and protect the confidentiality of medical information. ? Follow applicable infection-prevention and control procedures. ? Respond appropriately to suspected overdoses or adverse medical events, including administering naloxone when trained and authorized. ? Complete all required medication-awareness and overdose-response training. I. Communication & Interagency Collaboration Residential Support Workers must communicate respectfully, promptly, and professionally with residents, colleagues, supervisors, and external partners. Employees shall: ? Promptly report significant resident and operational concerns to management. ? Share relevant observations with Case Managers to support case planning and intervention. ? Liaise professionally with CSC, Parole Officers, institutional staff, healthcare and emergency services, police, and community-based service providers. ? title: Conseiller ou Conseillère - Gestion du sevrage résidentiel
description: Plusieurs postes occasionnels Postes syndiqués Le conseiller ou la conseillère en gestion du sevrage résidentiel est responsable de fournir des services non médicaux de gestion du sevrage à l'alcool et aux drogues aux clients du Centre de gestion du sevrage d'Ottawa (CGSO). Les services sont offerts à des personnes qui sont soit sous l'influence d'une substance ou ayant des symptômes de sevrage ou à des personnes qui passent à travers une période de crise les mettant à haut risque de rechute. Les soins cliniques offerts aux clients pendant leur séjour comprennent le dépistage initial, une évaluation, du suivi, des soins physiques ainsi que l'élaboration et la documentation d'un plan de soins et d'un plan de congé en collaboration avec le client. Le conseiller anime aussi des séances de counseling individuel ou de groupe et offre un soutien aux clients et aux membres de leur famille. Les services sont offerts en conformité avec les objectifs et les politiques du CGSO ainsi que les standards de gestion du sevrage de l'Ontario et du ministère de la Santé et des Soins de longue durée. Les candidats intéressés doivent être disponibles pour travailler des quarts de travail de jour, de soir et de nuit incluant les fins de semaines. Exigences : Diplôme d'études collégiales en travail social, toxicomanie, santé mentale ou services communautaires Niveau d'études souhaitable : Baccalauréat en travail social, psychologie, criminologie ou dans un domaine connexe de la toxicomanie Minimum de deux (2) ans d'expérience dans le domaine de la toxicomanie et/ou de santé mentale (une combinaison des deux serait souhaitable) Expérience en intervention, en entrevues et en counseling avec les clients qui souffrent de dépendances et / ou de problèmes de santé mentale Connaissance des techniques de counseling, des approches et des interventions présentement utilisées dans le domaine de la toxicomanie et de la santé mentale Bonne connaissance des symptômes de sevrage afin de gérer en toute sécurité les besoins physiques, mentaux et émotionnels des clients, en lien avec le sevrage à l'alcool et aux drogues Bonne connaissance des services de santé mentale, de toxicomanie, de soutien communautaire et des partenaires du secteur local de la région de Champlain Excellentes habiletés de communication orale et écrite, de niveau supérieur en français et en anglais Communication efficace axée sur le client Flexibilité et approche basée sur les besoins des clients Formation en intervention non-violente en situation de crise (INVSC), formation appliquée en techniques d'intervention face au suicide (ASIST/FATIS), formation RCR, entrevue motivationnelle, gestion des troubles concomitants, sont des atouts Preuve de vaccination complète contre la COVID-19 et l'hépatites B (obligatoire) CE QUE NOUS POUVONS VOUS OFFRIR : Salaire entre 28,60 $/h et 31,93 $/h Fonds de pension HOOP Pourcentage de salaire en lieu de bénéfices et vacances payées Opportunités de formation continue Programme d'aide aux employé(e)s et à la famille (PAESF) Milieu de travail francophone Faire partie d'une équipe multidisciplinaire et dynamique composée de professionnels d'expérience en toxicomanie et en santé mentale au sein d'une organisation en pleine croissance

title: Junior HSE Advisor
description: JUNIOR HSE ADVISOR At Platecon Projects Limited, safety is not only a core value, it is embedded in every action, program, plan, meeting and interaction we undertake. Our employees face challenging working environments every day and our commitment is to ensure everyone returns home safely, without incident. Platecon's health and safety program continues to evolve and improve every year, leading the way in the industry. We are now seeking an experienced, dedicated and passionate Junior HSE Advisor to join our innovative and dynamic team and continue to build on the success of our safety program. The Junior HSE Advisor will develop, implement, and maintain safety programs and procedures. You will work in cooperation with management, field employees and the Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committees/OHS Worker Representative to ensure our corporate, project and regulatory HSE commitments are met. Joining the team will not only provide challenging and rewarding work experiences, but also the opportunity to develop your career and contribute to a culture that values integrity, people, quality, community, and safety. Responsibilities: ? The role involves actively promoting awareness of the Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) program while fostering a proactive and positive safety culture across all levels of the organization. A key responsibility includes facilitating workplace safety and environmental inspections, such as Job Safety Analysis (JSA), Job Hazard Analysis (JHA), Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Toolbox Talks, and Safe Work Observations across all projects. This includes tracking corrective actions and maintaining thorough documentation. ?? The candidate will be responsible for coordinating safety meetings for both office and field staff, supporting management and supervisors in ensuring that all tasks are completed in compliance with corporate and project-specific HSE requirements. Conducting new hire safety orientations and performing regular inspections of personal protective equipment (PPE), lifting equipment, and other safety-related tools will be an integral part of the job. ? Ensuring that follow-up actions from inspections, audits, and investigations are documented and completed is essential. The role also includes participating in loss prevention initiatives and routinely observing on-site tasks to ensure adherence to all HSE standards. The candidate will assist with internal and external audits, including regulatory and COR® audits, and help identify HSE training needs, scheduling appropriate safety training for all staff. ?Additional duties include supporting the collection, tracking, and analysis of HSE performance indicators, as well as preparing and presenting detailed reports. The Junior HSE Advisor will participate in incident investigations, providing thorough analysis and documentation of findings. Completing HSE task logs and effectively communicating lessons learned from both internal and external investigations to staff are also important aspects of the role. Professional Experience and Qualifications: The successful candidate must have an HSE specific post-secondary degree/diploma or an equivalent level of education. Preference will be given to those with certified safety accreditations such as NCSO or CRSP, or progress towards. A strong knowledge of the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and its Regulations, the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) Act and regulations, as well as safety regulations relevant to Ontario construction, is essential. The candidate must be able to identify critical safety risks associated with tank construction, including hazards related to rigging, working at heights, hot work, and confined space entry. Proficiency in Microsoft Office software is required, and the ideal candidate will demonstrate excellent organizational skills and the ability to work well under pressure, managing multiple tasks and meeting deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, are necessary, along with well-developed presentation and public speaking abilities. Platecon Projects Limited, a RothLochston company, specializes in the design, construction, and repair of platework structures such as oil storage tanks, process vessels and stacks. Our services include engineering design, production of drawings, material procurement and field installation. Our dedicated team is committed to delivering high quality solutions for our clients while ensuring a safe and productive work environment for our people. For more information, please visit https://platecon.com/. ; If you are ready to join a collaborative and detail-oriented team, we want to hear from you. If you have any questions, please reach out to Alison Trimm at atrimm@rothlochston.com . Platecon Projects Limited is an equal opportunity employer seeking qualified candidates who will contribute to the diversification of our views and ideas.

title: Animal Health Technician
description: For 75 years, Charles River employees have worked together to assist in the discovery, development and safe manufacture of new drug therapies. Whether your background is in life sciences, finance, IT, sales or another area, your skills will play an important role in the work we perform. As an In Vivo Technician, you'll play a vital role in supporting scientific research while ensuring the highest standards of animal care and welfare. Whether you're a recent graduate looking to launch your career or an experienced animal care professional seeking your next opportunity, we'll provide the training, support, and career development you need to succeed. Administer test items and medications, including various injection techniques and gavage. Collect biological samples such as blood and urine. What We're Looking For You could be a great fit if you have: A Diploma in Animal Health, Environmental & Wildlife Management, Biotechnology, or a related field. A Bachelor's degree in Biology, Animal Science, or a related discipline. High school diploma, combined with either 2 to 3 years of experience as a Technical Assistant in a research center or 4 to 5 years of experience as a Technical Assistant in a veterinary clinic. Strong observation and problem-solving skills A genuine interest in animal welfare and scientific research The ability to perform physical work, including lifting up to 20 kg The ability to understand written English Please note that upon being hired, you will have to undergo an annual tuberculosis test covered by the company. Why Join Charles River? Competitive starting salary of $23.75/hour Evening, weekend, overtime, and holiday premiums Annual performance bonus Comprehensive benefits from day one Health & dental coverage Telemedicine access Free on-site gym (Senneville & Sherbrooke) 3 weeks vacation plus 5 personal days Training, mentorship, and career advancement opportunities Engaging employee events and activities Choose the Location That's Right for You Laval : 445 Boul. Armand-Frappier, Laval, QC, H7V 4B3 Senneville : 22022 route Transcanadienne, Senneville, QC, H9X 1C1 Sherbrooke :1580 rue Ida-Métivier, Sherbrooke (Fleurimont), QC, J1E 0B5 All locations offer free parking, EV charging stations, and convenient transportation options. Begin a Meaningful Career Where Science, Compassion, and Discovery Come Together Join a team that's helping bring tomorrow's treatments to life while making a positive impact on the health of communities worldwide. Apply today. This is Your Moment.

If you're ready to learn from experienced chefs, and build your career in one of Ottawa's most respected independent kitchens, we'd love to hear from you! Apply in confidence today. title: Infanteer (CAF)
employer: The Cameron Highlanders of Ottawa (Duke of Edinburgh's Own)
description: Infantry Soldiers are the Army's primary combat fighters and are responsible for closing with and engaging the enemy. They are the core members of the Combat Arms team, which includes Artillery and Armoured Soldiers. Infantry Soldiers are capable of operating anywhere in the world in any environment and in any combination of arms, including airmobile and amphibious operations. The primary duties of an Infantry Soldier are to: Expertly operate and maintain a wide range of weapons, including rifle, hand-grenades, light, medium and heavy machine-guns, and anti-tank weapons Use sophisticated equipment for field communications, navigation and night-vision surveillance Inspect and maintain weapon systems, vehicles, survival gear and personal defensive equipment Participate in airborne operations Operate with support elements such as fighter aircraft, tactical and artillery Engage in unarmed combat Employ camouflage and concealment, patrol, assault, defence, and escape-and-evasion tactics. Infantry Soldiers normally work outdoors. Both in training and on operations they live and work in conditions that would resemble those in the field. Infantry Soldiers will be posted to a battalion in Canada, but there are employment opportunities across Canada and on deployed operations around the world. To start a full or part-time career in the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) you must: Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident Be at least 18 years old (17 years old with parental consent), except: For the Paid Education programs - you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) For the Primary Reserves-you may be 16 years old (with parental consent) and must be enrolled as a full-time student Have completed at least Grade 10 or 24 credits of Secondary IV in Quebec (some jobs need higher levels of education) If you have completed your education outside Canada, you must have your Educational Credential Assessments (ECAs) completed for your high school and highest level of education prior to submitting your application. For more information about eligibility requirements or the application process, please visit Joining the Forces . You can submit your application even if you are not sure about the job-specific requirements. Once we get your application, we'll work with you to determine if you qualify. If you have questions at any time throughout the process or you'd like to know which part-time jobs are available in your area, you can visit our Help Centre or Contact Us .

title: Rehabilitation /Physiotherapy Assistant
description: Welcome to Ophysio! Company description We are a well established multidisciplinary practice in Orleans. We are looking for a dynamic person to join our team as a Rehab Assistant (RA) that will perform a variety of tasks for the clinic. They will be in contact with patients at the clinic helping to achieve the goal of fostering an environment that promotes patient comfort and trust. General Description As a student RA at Ophysio Clinic, you will play a combined role consisting of administrative and clinical work. The RA will be responsible with providing patient care as prescribed by the physiotherapist. You also will be responsible with maintaining the cleanliness of the clinic rooms and equipment as well as booking appointments for patients. The position is considered a crucial link between the patient and the care delivered by the practitioners. The incumbent must work collaboratively with all clinical services staff and patients exhibiting flexibility and a "can do" attitude. The position must exemplify the core values and mission of the organization, always exercising the utmost discretion, diplomacy and tact in patient-staff interactions. Specific Responsibilities Assist with conducting one-on-one physiotherapy treatments & exercises with assigned patients as directed by the Physiotherapist. Assign & encourage patients to reach the goals of their planned treatment programs. title: Early Childhood Educator (ECE) - Montessori Classroom Assistant & Elementary Support
description: Description Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is seeking an Early Childhood Educator to join our teaching team. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working with children across multiple age groups and appreciates the variety that comes with being part of a growing school. Working alongside experienced Montessori educators, the successful candidate will primarily support our Montessori Casa classrooms (ages 2.5 to 6 years), with opportunities to contribute to our lower elementary program and before and after school care, depending on qualifications, experience, and the needs of the school. Qualifications and experience in the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition (ISKCON) is an asset. The ideal candidate is charismatic, builds respectful relationships with children, has a natural ability to understand others' needs, is flexible and able to adapt to the needs of the program that come with working in a close-knit school community rather than that within a traditional school model. Responsibilities Responsibilities will vary based on qualifications and experience and may include: Support, create or implement a curriculum that promotes children's physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and practical life development. Lead or assist with the daily operation of a Montessori Casa classroom. Prepare and maintain a safe, organized, and engaging learning environment using Montessori principles and incorporating values of the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition. Observe children's interests, behaviour, and developmental progress, maintaining accurate records and documentation. Assess children's abilities and discuss observations and progress with families and colleagues. Support children's independence, concentration, confidence, and positive social interactions through respectful guidance. Guide children in developing practical life skills, self-care routines, conflict resolution, and self-regulation. Lead or participate in activities including storytelling, music, art, outdoor learning, movement Support lower elementary students with classroom routines and learning activities, where appropriate. Plan and organize activities for school-age children attending our before and after school program. Assist children with eating, dressing, toileting, diapering, handwashing, rest periods, and other daily care routines as needed. Prepare snacks and assist with meal routines. Maintain classroom materials, equipment, and learning resources. Ensure the health, safety, and well-being of all children while following licensing requirements and school policies. Communicate professionally with parents regarding children's daily experiences and developmental progress. Participate in staff meetings, collaborative planning, and ongoing professional development. About Our School Bhakta Prahlad Montessori School is an independent multi-age Montessori school located in Russell, Ontario. We currently operate three licensed Montessori Casa classrooms for children aged 2.5-6 years, offer before and after school care for neighbouring schools, and provide a multi-age elementary program. We have been operating for 10 years and continue to place an emphasis and value on genuine relationships. We believe in a holistic education model, nurturing mind, body and soul. The outstanding characters of the educators will be what shapes the character development of the children in their classrooms, and therefore we are looking for a unique individual to imbibe the teachings of bhakti and the qualities of a vaishnava. Educators have opportunities to contribute beyond a single classroom, share their individual strengths, and continue developing professionally as our programs evolve. Why Join Us? We're looking for someone who is seeking more than simply a job. We encourage initiative, offer regular professional development opportunities through our educational network, and provide the chance to take on increased responsibilities as our school continues to develop. If you're looking for a unique work environment, where relationships matter, and every day brings something a little different, we warmly invite your application. Qualifications Early Childhood Education Diploma (ECE) and registration (or eligibility for registration) with the College of Early Childhood Educators, or Montessori Certification, Teacher's Diploma, or Bachelor's Degree in Education with relevant experience Experience working within a school aligned with the bhakti tradition, including the ability to lead and teach daily mantra meditation and the study of vedic texts such as the Srimad Bhagavatam and Bhagavad-Gita Experience working with children Assets Experience working in a Montessori classroom Knowledge of Montessori pedagogy Knowledge of Vedic philosophy Experience volunteering/working in an ISKCON environment. Knowledge of Vaisnava culture; familiarity of its activities and operations Experience working with children across multiple age groups Ability to storytell, play and teach musical instruments, drama and visual arts Requirements CPR & First Aid (Level C) Vulnerable Sector Police Record Check Up-to-date immunizations (or valid exemption) Reliable transportation (public transportation to our location is limited) Job Type : Full-time Benefits Dental care Extended health care Paid time off Discounted or free meals Ability to Commute/Relocate Russell, ON K4R 1B8: Reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (required) Work Location : In person

title: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME)
description: Student Procurement Officer (PART TIME) Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC)/ Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) Student Procurement Officer Finance and Awards Administration Division National Capital Region NSERC and SSHRC are looking for a part-time student (15 to 22.5 hours per week) to support our Procurement and Contracting team. We are seeking a motivated, action-oriented team player who is interested in supporting a dynamic procurement environment and eager to develop new skills. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience while contributing to a collaborative and fast-paced team. Who we Are The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) funds visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will benefit our country. We are Canada's largest supporter of discovery and innovation. We work with universities, colleges, businesses and not-for-profits to remove barriers, develop opportunities and attract new expertise to make Canada's research community thrive. We give Canadian scientists and engineers the means to go further because we believe in research without borders and beyond frontiers. The Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) is the federal research funding agency that promotes and supports research and research training in the humanities and social sciences. Through its Talent, Insight and Connection programs, and through partnerships and collaborations, SSHRC strategically supports world-leading initiatives that reflect a commitment to ensuring a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC also oversees the delivery of a number of tri-agency programs, including the Canada Research Chairs and other research chairs programs, and the New Frontiers in Research Fund , which supports international, interdisciplinary, fast-breaking and high-risk research. Description of Duties Reporting to a Senior Procurement Advisor for the Procurement and Contracting group, the position provides contracting and procurement advice and services to Cost Centre (CC) Managers and Project Authorities (PAs) by planning and delivering the procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 for goods and below $40,000 for services) for low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services. This includes requirements such as call-ups against standing offers, low dollar value purchase orders; and requirements which fall under Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Shared Services Canada (SSC) for mandatory procurement instruments, including IT requirements. Responsibilities: Analyze client requirements, specification and requisition documents, review the adequacy of statements of work/ statements of requirements in order to plan and deliver procurement of low dollar value requirements (below $25,000 goods, $40,000 services) and low to medium complexity (risk) goods and services. Essential Qualifications Requirement: - must be returning to school in Winter term Official Language English essential Education Enrollment in a Supply Chain and Operations Management program (or equivalent) Experience Experience in a client service environment; Experience using Microsoft Office; Experience reviewing documentation; and Experience providing administrative support services Abilities Ability to plan/organize and address priorities Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing Ability to evaluate problems and suggest effective solutions Ability to analyze proposals and contractual documents Ability to work under pressure and with conflicting demands Ability to provide advice and guidance to clients Personal Suitabilities Strong interpersonal skills Client service orientation Results orientation Team-oriented Adaptable to ongoing change Autonomy, flexibility, accuracy, initiative and judgment Asset Qualifications Experience working in a procurement/financial system (such as SAP) Bilingual - Proficiency in both official languages Conditions of Employment • Adherence to the NSERC Code of Conduct; • Adherence to the NSERC Conflict of Interest and Post-Employment Policy; • Compliance with the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector; • Legal status to accept employment for the entire period of employment; and • Reliability security clearance Work Location Hybrid between telework and Zibi Building (125 Zaida Eddy Private, 5th floor, Ottawa ON) Should you be interested in this opportunity, please apply and submit your resume and cover letter through the Algonquin College HireAC portal. Your covering letter should clearly state why you would like this opportunity and how you meet the qualifications. We recommend using each of the experience factors as headers and provide clear and concrete examples and details of where, when and how you obtained the experience. For example, for each essential experience requirement, you should list where you gained the experience, your title at the time, a description of the tasks you performed relevant to the experience factor, and your accomplishments. We thank all those who apply. Only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. Security Clearance: Reliability status

title: Respiratory Therapist
employer: Saskatchewan Health Authority, North East, Recruitment & Retention
description: Description: Respiratory therapists evaluate, treat and manage patients of all ages with respiratory illnesses and other cardiopulmonary disorders in a wide variety of clinical settings. Respiratory therapists must demonstrate behavior and ethics that are consistent with the standards and ethics of all health care professionals. In addition to performing respiratory therapy procedures, Respiratory Therapists are involved in clinical decision making (such as patient evaluation, treatment selection and assessment of treatment efficacy) and patient education. Respiratory Therapists report directly to the Director of Respiratory Services. RRTs, as part of the Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA), work in hospital, clinical care and community care settings as part of a multidisciplinary health-care team in order to provide the best patient care. Hospital settings include Intensive Care Units (ICU), Neonatal ICU, Pediatric ICU, Emergency Departments, Critical Care Units, and other hospital wards. Community Care Settings include Home Oxygen Suppliers. RRTs work in shifts in order to provide health-care coverage based on the needs of the facility or clinic and this may include days, nights, and weekends. Opportunities to grow as a RRT include taking advanced courses to work in specialized areas and pursuing management and leadership positions. Pay, Incentives and Benefits: Wages: $38.64 - $47.14 /hr May be eligible for Recruitment Incentive up to $30,000 and Relocation up to $3,000 In addition to the above pay bands, the SHA provides a comprehensive benefits package including: Extended Health and Dental benefits Defined-Benefit Pension Plan Life and Disability Insurance Employee and Family Assistance Program Annual Vacation The Saskatchewan Health Authority is currently offering hiring incentives up to $30,000 plus relocation assistance of $3,000 may be available. Education Respiratory Therapy diploma (RT) Licenses Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certificate (ACLS) Basic Life Support Health Care Provider Certificate (BLS-HCP) Other Education and Training Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) Other Information Preference to HSAS members as per the SAHO/HSAS Collective Agreement Registered/eligible with the Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapist (CSRT)

title: Baker

title: Veterinary Technician
description: Join Our Team at Brockville Animal Hospital! Are you seeking a place that truly respects your professional journey, champions your growth, and values the balance between work and life? Brockville Animal Hospital, a thriving small-animal practice located in the heart of Ontario's stunning Thousand Islands region. This picturesque setting offers a perfect backdrop for maintaining that ideal work-life balance. Brockville's welcoming, friendly community is known for its relaxed pace, with no rush-hour traffic and easy access to outdoor activities such as camping, boating, river cruises, scuba diving, sports teams, and scenic parks. Efficient Workflow: We've mobilized our Registered Veterinary Technicians to elevate patient care and efficiency. With VetWise, our after-hour emergency system, you can count on excellent client support while protecting your downtime and work-life balance. Cutting-Edge Technology: Our Co.Vet system streamlines medical records, saving you time so you can focus on providing quality care and getting home on time. Team-Centric Mentorship and Growth At Brockville Animal Hospital, we foster a close-knit, supportive environment. Position: Veterinary Technician Hospital: Brockville Animal Hospital Location: Brockville, Ontario Job Type: Full-time Employment 35-40 hours/week What We Offer Wage rate commensurate with skillset & experience: $23.00/hr - $35.00/hr On-call shift premiums We offer a comprehensive health benefits package, including 50% of Medical, Dental, and Vision premiums covered by BAH. Our rotation includes shared evenings and weekends, with a day off provided in lieu for every other Saturday worked. Key Responsibilities Provide high-quality care to hospitalized and surgical patients Assist veterinarians during examinations, procedures, and surgeries Perform anesthesia induction, monitoring, and recovery Accurately prepare, and administer medications and vaccines Collect and process laboratory samples (blood, urine, feces, cytology) Take and process diagnostic imaging (radiographs) Maintain detailed and accurate medical records Educate clients on preventive care, treatment plans, and post-operative instructions Maintain a clean, safe, and organized clinical environment Follow all clinic protocols, health & safety standards, confidentiality, and regulatory requirements Qualifications & Requirements Ability to work collaboratively in a team-based environment Strong communication and client service skills Excellent organizational and multitasking abilities Compassionate, calm, and professional demeanor Ability to lift and restrain animals safely Experience in general practice / surgery / dentistry / anesthesia considered an asset Completion of the OAVT Professionalism & Ethics Workshop and planning to write the Veterinary Technician National Examination (VTNE) is an asset

title: Firearms Officer B/L

Please note: The successful candidate will be expected to work out of the Ottawa or Sudbury work location, five (5) days a week. We provide essential services that ensure the safety and security of the people of the Province of Ontario. The OPP is a division of the Ministry of the Solicitor General, the largest operational ministry in the province with a presence in every community across Ontario. We are the largest police service in Ontario and the second largest in Canada. The mandate of the Chief Firearms Office (CFO) is to protect public safety through the administration of the licensing provisions of the Firearms Act and Regulations. The Chief Firearms Officer for the Province of Ontario is delegated authority under the Act by the Minister of the Solicitor General, and is responsible for the administration and delivery of these key components of the Firearms Act. The OPP Values promote always doing the right things for the right reasons, by: Serving with PRIDE, PROFESSIONALISM and HONOUR. Interacting with RESPECT, COMPASSION and FAIRNESS. Leading with INTEGRITY, HONESTY and COURAGE. About the job Do you have the ability to deliver high?volume operational and administrative support in a dynamic environment, managing confidential information across multiple systems, responding to inquiries, and promoting firearms licensing through public outreach and education? In this exciting position you will process and assess firearms licence applications, transfers, and authorizations, by conducting detailed screenings, database reviews, and eligibility decisions to protect public safety. Additionally, you will act as a critical point of contact for the public, law enforcement, and justice partners, conducting interviews, responding to safety concerns, providing expert guidance on the Firearms Act, and supporting investigations and court processes. What you bring to the team Mandatory: Ability to pass an OPP background/ security investigation. Oral and written French Language skills at the advanced level Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Working knowledge of federal and provincial FOI requirements to ensure appropriate information sharing, along with strong understanding of the firearms licensing program to clearly explain eligibility and accurately direct inquiries. Proficiency with office and operational systems (e.g., Word, Excel, Outlook, CFIS, RMS, CPIC, Cognos) to accurately process applications, manage data entry, track application status, generate reports, and maintain organized records, along with effective use of standard office equipment. Interpersonal and Communication Skills You possess strong written, oral, listening, and interpersonal communication skills to prepare correspondence, respond to inquiries, provide clear and accurate information on the firearms licensing program, and collaborate effectively with internal teams and external partners. You are experienced in demonstrating tact, sensitivity, and professionalism when dealing with distressed, emotional, or irate individuals, and when communicating with ex?spouses, police services, and courts regarding licence?related matters. Problem Solving Skills You possess strong analytical and problem?solving skills to assess applicant eligibility, identify appropriate information sources and systems, conduct searches, verify documentation accuracy, and compile information for operational and court purposes. You possess effective decision?making and troubleshooting abilities to manage inquiries, resolve application or report discrepancies, address routine equipment or system issues, and determine when matters require escalation to supervisors or external agencies. Judgement and Discretion You have the ability to apply established firearms?licensing procedures and FOI guidelines to evaluate applications, make approval/refusal/referral decisions within authority, exercise discretion in information sharing, and escalate non?standard matters appropriately. You are able to manage and prioritize a high?volume, fast?paced workload by planning daily tasks, responding to changing demands, resolving client issues, and maintaining accuracy under frequent interruptions and competing priorities. You are proficient at communicating professionally and effectively in all interactions, preparing and editing documents and presentations, and exercising tact, diplomacy, and sound judgment when dealing with applicants, ex?spouses, law enforcement, and courts. Minden Animal Hospital - Minden, Ontario www.mindenanimalhospital.com Are you a recent RVT graduate looking for a supportive first job where you can grow your skills and feel truly valued? Minden Animal Hospital is excited to welcome a new or soon to be Registered Veterinary Technician to our team. We love teaching, we love mentorship, and we love helping new RVTs build confidence in a positive, team-focused environment. What You'll Get Here A friendly, collaborative team that supports each other Hands-on learning with experienced RVTs and veterinarians Opportunities to build skills in surgery, anesthesia, lab work, radiology, client communication, and patient care A workplace where your ideas, questions, and growth matter What You'll Do You'll be involved in all areas of patient care, including: General Technician Skills Talking with clients about vaccines, parasite prevention, nutrition, dental care, and wellness Helping clients understand medications and products Calculating drug dosages (with DVM double checks) Maintaining controlled drug logs Cleaning and sterilizing instruments and equipment Recording patient histories and communicating with owners Supporting a positive, team-oriented clinic culture Treatment Room Skills Collecting samples and running lab tests (hematology, biochemistry, microbiology, urinalysis, serology) Administering medications, vaccines, fluids, and treatments Providing nursing care to sick or injured patients Assisting with diagnostics and procedures using radiology and ultrasound Taking and processing radiographs Seeing patients for blood draws, bandage changes, vaccines, repeat imaging, medication refills, and more Supporting fellow technicians throughout the day Surgery Skills Administering fluids and blood products Monitoring anesthesia under veterinarian supervision Preparing patients, instruments, and equipment for surgery Ensuring anesthetic and monitoring equipment is functioning properly Assisting with surgical and diagnostic procedures Who We're Looking For Alumni, RVT new graduate, or recently licensed RVT Someone eager to learn, ask questions, and grow A team-player with a positive attitude Strong communication skills and a passion for patient care

title: Virtual Assistant
description: Julianna Banana offers culinary experiences for all ages. We offer hands-on cooking and baking workshops and events including birthday parties, private events, team-building experiences, youth summer camps, and so much more! We're passionate about creating fun, welcoming experiences that bring people together through food - and we're just as passionate about giving back to our community. A portion of our proceeds is donated to the Parkdale Food Centre, where we're proud to run many of our classes and be part of such an incredible community. We're a small but growing team, and we're always looking for enthusiastic, creative, hardworking people to teach and share their skills and who know how to spread the word about what we do, enjoy working with others, and want to help create memorable experiences for our guests. We're looking for a creative, organised and tech-savvy individual to join our growing business and to work with us on an ongoing basis across social media, website management, content creation, marketing and general digital/admin support. This is an ongoing freelance collaboration requiring approximately 8-10 hours of work spread-out in a week (sometimes more) This is a great opportunity to do something creative while learning skills. What You'll Be Working On: Social Media Create Instagram posts, Stories and Reels -Edit and prepare short-form video content Schedule and publish content Manage social media accounts -Respond to comments, messages and customer queries Create and adapt content Research trends, formats and content opportunities Help maintain a consistent visual identity and tone of voice across platforms Website Update and maintain our website -Create and edit page (knowledge of Wordpress Platform is a plus) Help identify website improvements General website management and organisation Content, Marketing & AI Write, create and send newsletters Research topics and content opportunities Use AI tools to create and enhance and improve our content and workflows Admin & Organisation Email management and basic customer communication Organise files, content and information Assist with planning and scheduling Research products, competitors, suppliers, tools and ideas Keep track of tasks and priorities Handle various online and administrative tasks as they arise You don't need to be an expert in every single area above. More importantly, we're looking for someone who is resourceful, creative, organised and comfortable figuring things out independently. You can lean more about who we are at www.juliannabanana.ca and on our socials @juliannabananabakewithme

title: Lighting Controls Technician (Building Automation Technician)
description: Join one of the brightest teams in the industry! Our client, located in Ottawa's West End, is experiencing exciting growth and is looking for a skilled Lighting Controls Technician (Building Automation Technician) to join their expanding team. Whether you're a recent graduate or an aspiring electronics professional eager to launch your career, this is a fantastic opportunity to gain hands-on experience and grow with an industry leader. This is an exciting field-based role that involves working directly with clients on-site to install, troubleshoot, and commission lighting control systems and applications. The position is highly mobile, with the majority of your time spent visiting customer locations rather than working from an office. Our client primarily works on projects throughout the Ottawa-Gatineau region, where team members are typically home every evening. Occasional travel to Northern Quebec may be required a few times per year for project assignments lasting up to one week. Duties may include but are limited to: Programming and commissioning lighting control panels Responding to service calls, performing system diagnostics, and troubleshooting issues Reviewing and interpreting plans and specifications for lighting control systems Developing and presenting lighting control system proposals to clients Managing maintenance contracts and ensuring timely delivery of services Performing other tasks as assigned to support the team and business operations Benefits and perks: Comprehensive health and dental benefits Pension matching program Monthly profit-sharing incentives Weekly perks: paid lunches every Friday and free snacks in the office Regular team-building activities to foster camaraderie Flexible scheduling to support work-life balance Opportunities for growth and advancement in a rapidly expanding organization Convenient free parking A dynamic and supportive work environment Contemporary and newly renovated office space Monday to Friday - 8:00am to 4:30pm (Fridays are 8:00am to 3:30pm) Salary: $60,000 to $75,000 per year depending on experience If you're a motivated and qualified candidate, please submit your resume in response to this posting. Additionally, please be prepared to provide 2 professional references upon request. We appreciate the interest of all applicants in Express Employment Professionals. Please note that only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Express Employment Professionals is an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applications from diverse candidates. Our selection process includes AI-enabled tools for screening based on keywords and minimum qualifications. A human decides who moves forward. Required skills and qualifications: Must be fluently bilingual (English / French) A diploma or degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Architectural Technician/Technologist or a related field or Building Automation System Operations certification Experience in servicing electronic and/or mechanical systems, preferably in the HVAC, robotics, or lighting industries is ideal but not required Strong computer skills, including: network fundamentals, software applications, hardware components Ability to work effectively in both independent and team-based settings Eligibility to obtain a Secret level Security Clearance

title: Multicultural Liaison Officer (MLO)
description: Position: Multicultural Liaison Officer (MLO) Term: 17.5 hours per week - September 2026 - June 25, 2027 Reports to: Manager of the Multicultural Liaison Officer Program Location: Various locations across the Ottawa region About OCISO OCISO supports immigrants through the journey of making Canada their home by providing creative and responsive programs that are culturally and linguistically appropriate, by building community through mutual respect and partnerships, and by fostering healthy and inclusive spaces for open dialogue and healing. Position Summary The Multicultural Liaison Officer (MLO) provides settlement service, needs assessment, information and orientation session and service referrals for immigrant and refugee children and youth and their families within Ottawa schools. The MLO collaborates with schools' administration and teachers to facilitate cross-cultural communication and ensure student integration and academic success. Main Responsibilities: • Conduct initial and periodic settlement needs assessments for immigrants and refugees • Provide settlement information, orientation, and referrals services for immigrants and refugees • Provide services in a supportive and culturally sensitive manner maintaining client confidentiality • Provide orientation about the Ontario education system to newcomer children, youth and families • Facilitate cross cultural communication between school administration and newcomer families • Assist with newcomer family parent/teacher interviews • Provide interpretation services to enable newcomer families to communicate with school administration on settlement related issues • Provide supports in the context of cross-cultural misunderstanding or lack of awareness between newcomer children, youth & families and school administration • Develop and present cultural competency workshops to school administration as required to ensure equity issues are addressed • Develop and present workshops to newcomer children, youth and parents to increase their knowledge of the Ontario education system • Advocate on client's behalf when appropriate • Support institutional and systemic changes required to ensure that newcomer children and youth achieve academic success Qualifications: • Post-secondary education in social sciences, education, or a related field • Knowledge and experience in community outreach and service delivery within the social service sector • Experience in working with newcomer communities • Proven ability to work effectively in a multi-disciplinary and multicultural team environment • Knowledgeable of the Ontario Education System and ideally, the Ottawa Carleton District School Board and Ottawa Catholic School Board policies and practises • Proven skills in workshop development and facilitation • Extensive knowledge of community resources • Proficiency with current computer applications including the MS Office Suite, internet-based productivity tools and databases • Self-motivated and able to work independently with minimal supervision • Excellent verbal and written knowledge of English & Arabic (mandatory), additional languages an asset.

title: Operations Assistant, Centretown Community Food Centre (CCFC)
description: The Centretown Community Food Centre is the community food bank that serves downtown Ottawa, providing food assistance to over 1,000 households each month. Job Title: Operations Assistant, Centretown Community Food Centre (CCFC) Under the general direction of the Manager, and working closely with the Operations Coordinator, has responsibility to open the Food Centre and receive food orders, ensuring the accuracy compared with the order. Also, leads volunteers to ensure food is ready for client service. Under the supervision of the Operations Coordinator, registers clients for service about 2-3 times a week. Specific responsibilities include: Arrive between 8-8:30 to open the food centre, accept food deliveries and greet volunteers; Put the client sign-in sheet out in the lobby area at 8-8:30; Distribute numbers to clients on the sign-in sheet at 11:20-30; Supervise and lead volunteers in ensuring food centre shelves are fully stocked and prepared for client service; In conjunction with the Manager and Operations Coordinator, ensure food safety guidelines are being followed at all times; Meet, sign for and check for completeness of all food orders from sources such as the Ottawa Food Bank and grocery stores; Accept, note down and ensure proper sorting of all food received from community food drives and other food donations; Conduct Client intake 2-3 times a week; Assist in smooth operations with continual restocking, cleaning and rotating of food products during client service. Hours: The Operations Assistant is expected to work part-time at approximately 25 hours/ week, on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday starting between 8:00-8:30 AM Desired skills and abilities include: Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to work with diverse clients, staff; Strong organization skills; Demonstrated reliability and flexibility to accommodate a changing environment; Ability to work as a team and to be comfortable in a leadership role; Ability to safely lift 40 lbs; Full English fluency and communications required, French an important asset and fluency in other languages is highly valuable.

title: IT Technician, Creativity Centre - Community Engagement
description: Career Opportunity: H alton Hills Public Library IT Technician, Creativity Centre - Community Engagement One (1) Permanent Part-Time Position Job Number: 202611 The Town of Halton Hills is located on the Treaty Lands and Territory of the Mississauga of the Credit. Halton Hills, located 45 minutes from Toronto, is a unique and vibrant community with over 61,000 people and two well-established library branches. HHPL welcomes more than 250,000 visitors annually and more than 500,000 website visitors. We empower our patrons to learn, read, create, innovate, and experience at our library. We strive to remove barriers and to foster an atmosphere of learning, support, understanding and inclusion. We employ over 35 professionally trained library staff, who go above and beyond to provide stellar service to our patrons and deliver high-quality programs and relevant events. If this excites you, we'd love to continue the conversation. Position Summary The Halton Hills Public Library is seeking an Information Technology Technician who will provide training and support to staff and members of the public to ensure customer service excellence, while bringing a hands-on, experimental approach to learning and a "tinkerer" mindset, with a strong interest in exploring, testing, and troubleshooting using tools and emerging technologies. The Information Technology Technician will provide customer service and support for new technologies for all ages. The position will plan, coordinate, and conduct all ages programming and training sessions on the use of makerspace technologies and consumer devices to support staff and patron knowledge. In addition, they may be called upon to actively resolve end user help requests both in-person, via email or by telephone and work on a public service desk and help patrons of all ages and backgrounds make the greatest use of the library by providing in-depth information, service and advice on print and non-print collections. This position will work out of the Georgetown and Acton Branches and is required to work weekdays, evenings, and weekends. The position will report to the Youth Services Librarian. Position Details These responsibilities indicate the general nature and level of work expected. It is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required by the incumbent. The incumbent may be asked to perform other duties as required and as the nature of library services evolve. Champion and promote new makerspace technologies and consumer devices to the public and staff Process, plan and provide on-site technology certification and other programs Instruct the public and staff in the use of technology for our Makerspace (Creativity Centre) such as 3D printing, Adobe Creative Cloud, sewing and embroidery machines, and Cricut. Instruct the public and staff in the use of makerspace technologies, consumer devices and social media Develop help sheets and frequently asked questions lists for end users Field incoming help requests from members of the public via email, telephone, and Book a Librarian service in a courteous manner Apply diagnostic utilities to aid in troubleshooting, and machine maintenance in consultation with the I.T. Specialist Plan, conduct and evaluate creative, cultural, dynamic, innovative, and literacy-building programs for all ages, as well as library programming on Makerspace technologies, social media, e-resources, and desktop software Represent the Library at outside events and to community organizations (local events, schools, community centres) Instruct the public and staff in the use of the catalogue and the Library's other online resources such as our website and databases Assist with the development of Makerspace procedures Assist in supervising the work of Community Engagement summer students Serve as a member of the Emerging Technology Committee Perform other job-related duties Hours: Approx. 28 hours per week. Includes weekdays, evenings and weekends in both Acton and Georgetown Branches or at event locations. Compensation: The rate for this position is $36.38 to $43.31 per hour Position Details: This posting is for an existing vacancy in the Community Engagement department Application Deadline: September 27, 2026 at 11:59 pm Start Date: October 2026 Qualifications Essential Minimum education: A Diploma in Computer Science/Information Science or equivalent 6 months - 1 year experience working in a similar position, or equivalent education and experience Superb customer service skills Excellent attention to detail Well-developed library-programming and presentation skills Able to accommodate a variable schedule Able to organize time efficiently Ability to interact pleasantly and courteously with the public and staff, and to promote a harmonious workplace Strong written and oral communication skills. Desirable Additional training in Library techniques or related disciplines Keen interest in emerging technology trends and continuous learning Valid driver's license Access to a vehicle

title: Registered Practical Nurse
description: Perform nursing procedures consistent with the Standards of Practice and Scope of Practice as defined by the College of Nurses of Ontario. Responsible for administration of medications including narcotics, catheter insertion, maintenance, troubleshooting and discontinuation, wound care; developing appropriate treatments in collaboration with wound care team, ongoing monitoring and evaluation, escalation based on assessments if worsening condition, respiratory assessments leading to initiation of oxygen therapy and medication interventions, documentation in the resident's electronic health record including, progress notes, medication administration and effectiveness, interventions and changes in conditions. Complete all vital signs including neurological. Assist with the assessment of the residents' needs, their plan of care and evaluation of the care provided. Partner with residents and their families in the provision of care. Provide for the residents' emotional and physical comfort and safety. Assess the residents and report significant change(s) in condition to the Registered Nurse. Maintain responsibility for the residents unless the care needs are outside of their scope of practice. Work in collaboration with the Registered Nurse and Physicians to make modifications to resident care plans and treatments as required. Complete appropriate referrals to interdisciplinary team in accordance with the plan of care or changes in resident condition. Perform health training to residents within the realm of his/her knowledge and training. Direct the Personal Support Workers to assist with social or recreational activities for residents. Responsible for personal and vocational growth and development, while remaining up to date on best practice guidelines. Possess strong interpersonal and communication skills with exceptional organizational and leadership ability. • Provide nursing care to residents with acute and chronic illnesses and conditions whose needs are generally stabilized. The RPN will assume the role of team leader per neighborhood, guiding and directing the Personal Support Workers in the provision of high quality and safe resident care. • Two (2) year diploma Registered Nursing Assistant/Registered Practical Nurse and CPR as a part of the core program. Current registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario in good standing. • Minimum of six (6) months' experience required.

title: Diagnostic Medical Sonographer (Ultrasound Technologist)
description: At Canada Diagnostic Centres ("CDC"), we are driven by helping Canadians access diagnostic services and providing remarkable experiences to our patients every day. Our care is compassionate, accurate and timely to help patients make progress in their health journey. We live by our vision of "Remarkable Care. Remarkable Careers." We are looking for recent or upcoming Diagnostic Medical Sonography graduates who are eligible for or registered with the ACMDTT to join our expanding outpatient clinics as full-time, part-time, or casual Ultrasound Technologists. Working collaboratively with radiologists and other healthcare professionals, you'll explain procedures, position patients, adjust equipment, and capture diagnostic images. Bringing compassion and clarity to each patient interaction, you'll help ensure remarkable care every visit. What You'll Be Doing Perform Ultrasound Exams: Conduct routine and specialized sonography imaging under the direction of Radiologists and referring Physicians, while adhering to departmental protocols and guidelines. Provide Remarkable Care: Explain exams and procedures, address questions, ease concerns, and help patients feel comfortable. Collaborate with Clinic Teams: Partner with radiologists and other teams to help deliver a seamless and thoughtful experience. Expand Expertise: Engage in ongoing professional development to refine existing skills, build new competencies, and specialize in additional skillsets such as Interventional, MSK, and Breast. Ensure Compliance: Follow privacy, confidentiality, safety, and other regulatory requirements. Monitor and Troubleshoot Systems: Track ultrasound equipment performance, document findings, and resolve basic issues. Prepare and Maintain Work Areas: Prepare and stock exam rooms for exams and procedures; report low inventory as needed. What We're Looking For Professional Membership: Current registration, or eligibility, with the Alberta College of Medical Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technologists (ACMDTT), or eligibility for registration. Ultrasound Experience: Clinical competency as a generalist sonographer, with an interest in refining and expanding skills in advanced practice areas such as MSK, OB/GYN, vascular and cardiac exams, and interventional procedures. A Compassionate Approach: A history of remarkable care, collaboration, adaptability, and flexibility. What We Offer Competitive Pay: Industry-leading wages and unique additional earning opportunities. Sign-On Bonus: A welcome incentive for joining our team (terms and conditions apply). Relocation Allowance: Financial assistance for eligible candidates to help with moving expenses. Generous Time Off: Vacation, personal days, sick leave, and paid time off for your birthday for full-time and part-time team members. Casual team members receive vacation pay. Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision benefits, plus access to our Employee & Family Assistance Program (terms and conditions apply). Learning & Development: Specialized training opportunities, along with an annual education allowance for part-time and full-time team members. Long-Term Savings Program: RRSP/TFSA plan (terms and conditions apply). Income Protection: Short-term and long-term disability coverage available for part-time and full-time team members. Life Insurance: Coverage to protect you and your loved ones (terms and conditions apply). Professional Licensing Support: Funding available for Sonography Canada and ACMDTT membership fees. Additional Information Students and Recent Graduates: We welcome applications from Diagnostic Medical Sonography students completing their studies in 2026, 2027, or 2028, as well as recent graduates who completed their studies in 2025 and 2026! Position Types: Full-time, part-time or casual options to align with your schedule and career goals. Consistent Schedule: Daytime, Monday to Friday. Work Location: Clinic assignments will be discussed during the candidacy process and guided by operational needs and professional development, with preferences considered where possible. Out-of-Province Applicants: Eligibility for registration with the ACMDTT is required. About Canada Diagnostic Centres With a network of over 50+ community clinics across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Ontario, we have been a leader and innovator in radiological services for more than 30 years. At the core of our work is a simple belief: Clarity Through Caring. This means diagnostic imaging that is compassionate, accessible, and grounded in quality. In 2025, we supported more than 900,000 patients through their diagnostic journey. Our expertise spans a full range of imaging and interventional services, including MRI, CT, Ultrasound, Echocardiography, Nuclear Medicine, Mammography, X-Ray, Breast Imaging, Bone Mineral Density, Fluoroscopy, Maternal Fetal Medicine, Pediatric Imaging, Gastrointestinal Studies, and image-guided pain management procedures. Our services are delivered by collaborative interdisciplinary teams that bring clarity through caring to life. Inspired by what our teams make possible, we create opportunities for development, provide reliable equipment, and continuously improve how care is delivered. The care we extend to our patients and teams shapes how we welcome applicants. We actively invite applications from all individuals and are committed to equitable hiring practices. If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please contact us at talentacquisition@canadadiagnostics.ca. Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. All applicants must have legal authorization to work in Canada.

description: Medical Radiation Technologist (MRT) 2 Full Time Positions & Part - Time Career Opportunities Monday - Friday Day Shifts $43.27hr Why KOPI?
