You'll work in a two-person team responding to calls from hospitals, retirement homes, and private residences across Ottawa - treating every decedent, and every family, with the dignity they deserve. About EORS Since 2003, Eastern Ontario Removal Services has been the National Capital Region's leading removal service for the funeral industry - the largest and longest-running provider in Ottawa. Our unmarked, professionally equipped fleet and trusted relationships with funeral homes, hospitals, and police services are built on one thing: staff who show up with compassion, integrity, and respect every time. Why Join Our Team Paid, hands-on training - no prior experience required Security clearance fully paid for by the company Full-time or part-time schedule Health benefits: dental, vision, and life insurance (for eligible employees working 20hrs a week) Work as part of a supportive two-person team, never alone on a call A genuinely meaningful role - you make a difficult moment easier for grieving families A Day in the Life You'll work 12-hour on-call shifts in pairs. When a call comes in, the dispatcher sends you the details and your team heads to the scene - a hospital, home, or care facility. You'll carry out the removal with care and professionalism, then transport the decedent to different locations for after care. What You'll Do Complete removals of decedents from hospitals, private residences, and retirement/nursing homes Safely operate company vehicles to transport human remains Offer calm, compassionate support to grieving families at the scene Complete funeral home intake paperwork accurately Coordinate with funeral home staff, police, and dispatchers throughout your shift What We're Looking For A kind, presentable, and professional demeanor Strong interpersonal and communication skills Ability to lift up to 100 lbs. and push/pull up to 250 lbs. Comfortable working outdoors in all weather, and available for nights/weekends Good organizational and time-management skills Valid G2 or G driver's licence Clean criminal record French is an asset, not required Compensation & Benefits Competitive hourly wage (training $20 per hr. Wages increase after probation, and again every 6 months up till 2 years of employment) Dental care, vision care, and life insurance Flexible scheduling Paid security clearance and training How to Apply If you're reliable, compassionate, and ready to do work that truly matters, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today with your resume to Lacey@eors.email

title: Dental Hygienist Level 1
description: Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to supporting the health and wellbeing of our military members. Position Overview As a Dental Hygienist at CFB Ottawa, you'll play a critical role in delivering high-quality oral healthcare to the men and women of the Canadian Armed Forces. Working alongside skilled dentists, you'll be a part of a close-knit team focused on supporting the health, well-being, and readiness of Canada's military members. Looking for that work/life balance? This opportunity offers daytime hours only-no evenings, no weekends, and you'll be off for all provincial stat holidays. On top of that, we're offering group benefits program with access to paramedical services and more. You'll also have access paid time off! Responsibilities • Perform scaling, root planning, curettage, polishing procedures, desensitizing agents, occlusal sealants and anti-cariogenic agents • Provide oral hygiene instructions, nutritional counselling and smoking cessation • Conduct periodontal examinations and record clinical findings • Take digital radiographs • Provide administrative support such as updating patient databases, scheduling programs, and maintaining patient records Qualifications • Graduate of an accredited Dental Hygiene program • Registered and in good standing within the province of Ontario (CDHO) • CPR Level C or BLS provider • WHMIS Certification Additional Requirements • Eligible to obtain a Government Security Clearance at the Reliability level Compensation $43 - 46/ hour Vacancy 1 • Graduate of an accredited Dental Hygiene program • Registered and in good standing within the province of Ontario (CDHO)

title: Sonographer Part-Time
description: Almonte General Hospital and Carleton Place & District Memorial Hospital created the Mississippi River Health Alliance (MRHA) in 2016 to formalize their commitment to work together to improve each patient and resident's overall health care experience through a strong, coordinated system of care. An integrated Senior Team leads the two Hospitals, as well as Fairview Manor and Lanark County Paramedic Service which are operating divisions of AGH. Over 600 caring staff, physicians and midwives provide excellent primary, acute and long-term care to citizens of Lanark County, West Ottawa and Renfrew County. The Sonographer produces quality sonographic images on PACS in accordance with Sonography Canada and the College of Medical Radiation and Imaging Technologists of Ontario to ensure accurate diagnosis and treatment for all patients. The incumbent must be a member of Sonography Canada and CMRITO. The Almonte General Hospital/MRHA offers: Competitive Salaries Pension Plan (Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan - HOOPP) Employee and Family Assistance Program …and so much more! Ability to meet all demands of the job, both physical and cognitive Ability to work cooperatively and respectfully within a team environment. Must have a satisfactory performance and attendance records Ability to work in a manner that is in compliance with patient/resident and employee safety practices, policies and procedures of the organization. Ability to contribute to a work environment that is conducive to the organizations Workplace Violence and Harassment policy. Mandatory Requirements Current Registration with Sonography Canada and a maintained registry status by obtaining the required 40 hours Continuing Medical Education credits every three years Graduate of an approved Diagnostic Sonography Course Minimum of two (2) years' experience, preferred Must be able to perform Obstetrical Ultrasounds and current experience in Vascular Ultrasounds would be a definite asset. Current CPR

title: Maintenance Technician
description: It is a great time to join the Saand team! As a leading glass fabrication Company with 4 facilities (Brockport, Rexdale, London and Ottawa,) we are always looking for first class talent to drive results! WHAT WE DO Founded in 1990, Saand has become the leading glass supplier of commercial and residential Insulated Glass Units, fabricated OEM office furniture components, as well as a major distributor of float glass, laminated glass and mirror in North America. WHY APPLY WITH US? Saand employees enjoy: A company culture and environment that promotes engagement, innovation, inclusion and creativity allowing employees to achieve results! Employee recognition programs with incentives, and the opportunity for growth Not to mention, Saand offers a full and comprehensive benefit package including: Competitive salary Single & family company health & dental benefits Long Term Disability, Life and AD&D insurance RRSP/DPSP Safety boots and prescription safety eye wear entitlement POSITION: Maintenance Technician: Afternoon shift starts 3:30pm LOCATION: Ottawa Facility (2448 Huntley Road, Stittsville, ON) PURPOSE OF POSITION: As the PM Technician you will function in providing both a reactive and proactive, multi-skilled maintenance service on all operational equipment and facilities infrastructure, ensuring that Health, Safety and Environmental requirements are adhered to. Implement and manage continuous improvement and modern manufacturing principals by highlighting deficiencies and recommending changes in training, working practices and processes. RESPONSIBILITIES: Ensures operation of machinery and mechanical equipment by completing preventive maintenance requirements on motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, and production machines; following diagrams, sketches, operations manuals, manufacturer's instructions, and engineering specifications; troubleshooting malfunctions Responds to emergency break downs during the production process. Removes defective parts by dismantling devices; using hoists, cranes, and hand and power tools; determines changes in dimensional requirements of parts by inspecting used parts; using rules, calipers, micrometers, and other measuring instruments. Controls downtime by informing production workers of routine preventive maintenance techniques; monitoring compliance. Fabrication and modification of new and existing equipment Maintain/calibrate measuring tools and equipment. Ensures machinery is locked out in accordance with legislated requirements and the Occupational Health and Safety Act. JOB REQUIREMENTS: Ability to build and repair a variety of mechanical systems Knowledge of computerized machinery Ability to read blueprints and technical specifications Ability to weld effectively Flexibility to work overtime or weekends REQUIREMENTS: 2-3 years of Maintenance Technician experience in a manufacturing plant Saand is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. If you are selected to participate in the recruitment process, please inform Human Resources of any accommodations you may require. Saand will work with you in an effort to ensure that you are able to fully participate in the process

title: Respiratory Therapist
employer: Saskatchewan Health Authority, North East, Recruitment & Retention
description: Description: Respiratory therapists evaluate, treat and manage patients of all ages with respiratory illnesses and other cardiopulmonary disorders in a wide variety of clinical settings. Respiratory therapists must demonstrate behavior and ethics that are consistent with the standards and ethics of all health care professionals. In addition to performing respiratory therapy procedures, Respiratory Therapists are involved in clinical decision making (such as patient evaluation, treatment selection and assessment of treatment efficacy) and patient education. Respiratory Therapists report directly to the Director of Respiratory Services. RRTs, as part of the Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA), work in hospital, clinical care and community care settings as part of a multidisciplinary health-care team in order to provide the best patient care. Hospital settings include Intensive Care Units (ICU), Neonatal ICU, Pediatric ICU, Emergency Departments, Critical Care Units, and other hospital wards. Community Care Settings include Home Oxygen Suppliers. RRTs work in shifts in order to provide health-care coverage based on the needs of the facility or clinic and this may include days, nights, and weekends. Opportunities to grow as a RRT include taking advanced courses to work in specialized areas and pursuing management and leadership positions. Pay, Incentives and Benefits: Wages: $38.64 - $47.14 /hr May be eligible for Recruitment Incentive up to $50,000 and Relocation up to $3,000 In addition to the above pay bands, the SHA provides a comprehensive benefits package including: Extended Health and Dental benefits Defined-Benefit Pension Plan Life and Disability Insurance Employee and Family Assistance Program Annual Vacation Education Respiratory Therapy diploma (RT) Licenses Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certificate (ACLS) Basic Life Support Health Care Provider Certificate (BLS-HCP) Other Education and Training Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) Other Information Preference to HSAS members as per the SAHO/HSAS Collective Agreement Registered/eligible with the Canadian Society of Respiratory Therapist (CSRT)

title: Immigration Law Clerk/Paralegal
description: At Green and Spiegel, the title of the role is Immigration Case Analyst. Green and Spiegel, Canada's preeminent immigration law firm, sets the gold standard in the highly specialized area of immigration law. With a team of 120 talented individuals, the firm guarantees that each and every client receives top notch service. Given the breadth and depth of expertise at Green and Spiegel, there is no case too complicated or too large for the firm to handle. The firm reflects the diversity of the clients they serve and can provide services in approximately 30 languages. Knowing that you have a significant role in helping people at a critical point in their lives, makes working at Green and Spiegel a very exciting and rewarding place to work. Come join the team! The Immigration Case Analyst plays a key role in the intake, processing and follow up of client files. Immigration Case Analysts operate at various levels of autonomy and on various types of immigration files depending on their level of experience and tenure with the Firm. If you are someone who is eager to learn, values teamwork and strives for excellence in all that you do, then Green and Spiegel will be a great place for you. We are seeking a legal professional with any level of previous experience at an immigration law firm and someone who thrives working on challenging and rewarding work in a fast-paced environment. Experience with the following immigration application types would be an asset: LMIAs Work Permits Sponsorships Express Entry Investor Programs Immigration Case Analysts may report into a Team Lead, Associate Lawyer or Partner depending on the level and team. Key Duties and Responsibilities: Acting as the key point of contact for client inquiries at all stages; sending out initiation for files and providing clients with status updates throughout the life-cycle of their file Completing government forms required for various applications, drafting submission letters, mining the client's file for information and following up on outstanding information in a timely manner Conducting research and leveraging government resources to ensure processes are current and appropriate documents are being used Full accountability of assigned files or applications including checking client ledgers and billing processes, reviewing invoices for approval Scheduling appointments and meetings with clients Ensuring that timelines and deadlines are diarized and met including expiry dates and other key dates Skills and Qualifications: Bachelor's degree OR a Diploma or Certificate is required Any legal administrative or immigration experience including LMIA, Express Entry, PNP, Sponsorship and Work Permit Applications is an asset Excellent customer service skills Strong attention to detail and organizational abilities Excellent writing abilities is a requirement Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-volume environment

description: Position Overview The Assistant Manager is generally responsible for assisting with the day-to-day operations of the store as assigned by the Dealer-Owner or Store Manager. These duties commonly include supervision of personnel, serving as manager in the manager's absence, helping to meet sales and financial objectives, advertising and promotional planning, working on special projects, supervising inventory, merchandising, pricing, and facilitating communications between management and employees. The Assistant Manager performs all assigned tasks with sufficient speed and accuracy to support store efficiency and a high level of customer service. title: Community and Fund Development Lead
description: Position Summary The Community & Fund Development Lead is responsible for coordinating and implementing fund development and community engagement strategies that generate sustainable revenue, foster meaningful community relationships, and increase awareness of the North Okanagan Hospice Society (NOHS). This position supports the organization's mission by delivering high-quality fundraising initiatives, donor stewardship programs, grant activities, community partnerships, events, and communications that align with the Society's strategic priorities. The position builds and maintains strong relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, and supporters while ensuring an exceptional donor and community experience. Working collaboratively across the organization, the position contributes to a culture of teamwork, innovation, and service excellence. As a member of a small non-profit organization, the position provides support to organizational initiatives as required, with all responsibilities contributing to revenue generation, donor stewardship, community engagement, or increased awareness of Hospice services. Key Responsibilities Fund Development & Donor Relations Coordinate the implementation of the Society's annual fund development strategy in alignment with organizational goals and fundraising targets. Build, cultivate, solicit, and steward meaningful relationships with individual donors, sponsors, foundations, service clubs, businesses, and community partners. Identify, develop, and secure new funding opportunities, including major gifts, grants, sponsorships, and community partnerships. Coordinate annual giving initiatives including direct mail campaigns, online fundraising, monthly giving, memorial giving, and other donor engagement campaigns. Develop and implement donor stewardship initiatives that foster long-term relationships, meaningful recognition, and donor retention. Maintain accurate donor records and fundraising data within the donor management system while monitoring fundraising performance and preparing reports as required. Monitor fundraising budgets and campaign performance to maximize revenue generation and return on investment. Strategic Fund Development, Planning & Evaluation Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Society's annual fund development plan in alignment with strategic priorities and revenue goals. Monitor and evaluate fundraising campaigns, donor engagement activities, and community initiatives using key performance indicators and fundraising metrics. Analyze fundraising data, donor trends, and campaign outcomes to identify opportunities for growth, innovation, and continuous improvement. Prepare reports, summaries, and recommendations to support informed decision-making by the Executive Director and Board of Directors. Identify emerging fundraising trends, community needs, and best practices to strengthen the Society's fund development strategies and long-term sustainability. Support the development of annual fundraising goals, campaign calendars, and project timelines to ensure coordinated implementation of fund development activities. Foster a culture of continuous improvement by evaluating the effectiveness of fundraising initiatives and recommending enhancements to maximize community engagement and revenue generation. Grants & Sponsorship Development Research, identify, and pursue government, corporate, foundation, and community grant opportunities that align with organizational priorities. Prepare compelling grant proposals, applications, supporting documentation, and required reporting to funding agencies. Maintain an annual grants calendar to ensure timely submission, reporting, and stewardship of grant-funded initiatives. Develop sponsorship opportunities and customized sponsorship packages that create value for community partners while supporting organizational fundraising objectives. Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with current and prospective sponsors to encourage long-term investment in the Society's mission. Fundraising Events & Community Engagement Coordinate the planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the Society's fundraising events and community engagement initiatives. Lead the coordination of signature fundraising events including Dancing with the Vernon Stars, Hike for Hospice, the Butterfly Release, Kentucky Derby Gala, and other fundraising initiatives as assigned. Support third-party fundraising events and community-led initiatives that benefit the Society. Recruit, orient, coordinate, and recognize volunteers supporting fundraising events in collaboration with the appropriate organizational lead. Represent the Society at community events, networking opportunities, presentations, and stakeholder meetings, promoting the mission and values of Hospice. Foster positive relationships within the community that strengthen awareness, engagement, and support for Hospice services. Marketing, Communications & Public Awareness Coordinate fund development marketing and communication initiatives that increase community awareness, donor engagement, and support for the Society. Develop and maintain engaging content across the Society's social media platforms, ensuring consistent branding, messaging, and storytelling. Collaborate on fundraising campaigns, promotional materials, newsletters, donor communications, and digital marketing initiatives. Support media relations by preparing media releases, public announcements, promotional content, and community communications as required. Monitor communication and social media performance using analytics and engagement metrics to evaluate effectiveness and inform future strategies. Ensure all marketing and communications reflect the values, mission, and visual identity of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Collaboration & Organizational Support Work collaboratively with the Executive Director, program leaders, administrative staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to advance the Society's mission. Participate actively in staff meetings, strategic planning, training, and organizational initiatives. Support an integrated approach to fundraising, communications, volunteer engagement, programs, and community outreach. Foster a respectful, compassionate, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace. Maintain confidentiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards in all interactions. Exercise sound judgment and responsibly manage organizational resources within approved budgets. Provide support during periods of increased organizational activity while maintaining focus on the primary responsibilities of the role. Perform other duties consistent with the purpose, scope, and evolving needs of the position. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Education, Training and Experience Required Qualifications: Diploma or bachelor's degree in Fund Development, Business Administration, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Non-Profit Management, or a related discipline is preferred. An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered. Minimum of three (3) years' experience in fund development, donor relations, community engagement, marketing, communications, event management, or a related field, preferably within the non-profit sector. Demonstrated experience coordinating fundraising campaigns, donor stewardship initiatives, sponsorship development, and community events. Experience researching, writing, and managing grant applications and funding reports. Experience developing marketing and communication materials, including digital and social media content. Experience using donor management (CRM) databases to maintain records, generate reports, and support fundraising activities. Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and competing priorities. Experience working collaboratively with volunteers, community partners, sponsors, and diverse stakeholder groups. Experience working in a hospice, healthcare, or not-for-profit environment is preferred Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and relevant administrative systems Intermediate knowledge of computer hardware and software functions Attention to detail and accuracy required Clear Criminal Record Skills and Attributes: Cultural Competency: Demonstrates respect, sensitivity, and understanding of diverse cultural perspectives and practices. Builds inclusive relationships with donors, volunteers, community partners, and stakeholders while promoting equitable access and participation in Hospice programs and services. Relationship Building : Establishes, cultivates, and sustains positive relationships with donors, sponsors, volunteers, community partners, staff, and Board members. Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, and exceptional donor stewardship while fostering long-term community support for the Society. Communication: Communicates effectively with clarity, professionalism, empathy, and authenticity across diverse audiences. Demonstrates exceptional written communication skills, including grant writing, donor communications, marketing materials, and social media content. Confidently represents the Society through presentations, networking opportunities, and community engagement activities. Collaboration & Teamwork: Works collaboratively with staff, volunteers, Board committees, and community partners to achieve shared organizational goals. Fosters a respectful, inclusive, and supportive team environment while contributing positively to organizational culture. Initiative & Innovation: Demonstrates creativity, resourcefulness, and a proactive approach to identifying new fundraising opportunities, community partnerships, and donor engagement strategies. Applies sound problem-solving, decision-making, and critical thinking skills to improve programs and achieve organizational objectives. Planning & Organization: Demonstrates exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple fundraising campaigns, grants, events, and competing priorities while consistently meeting deadlines and maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Analytical Thinking & Results Orientation : Uses fundraising data, donor insights, and performance metrics to evaluate outcomes, identify trends, and recommend continuous improvements. Demonstrates accountability for achieving fundraising goals while supporting the Society's long-term sustainability. Self-Management: Demonstrates resilience, adaptability, accountability, and sound judgment while managing competing priorities in a dynamic non-profit environment. Maintains confidentiality, professional boundaries, and a commitment to continuous learning and professional growth. Attitude: Models a positive, enthusiastic, and professional attitude that reflects the mission, vision, and values of the North Okanagan Hospice Society. Demonstrates compassion, integrity, and a genuine commitment to building meaningful relationships and strengthening community support for Hospice services. 2 - 3 years of experience

title: Vice-President, Revenue and Strategic Partnerships
description: Title Vice-President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships Type Permanent, Full-time, 35 hours per week Location Ontario (Toronto, Ottawa) Reports to President & CEO Salary $150,000-185,000 About Us Kinvia, previously known as Canadian Feed the Children, envisions a world in which children, youth, and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Kinvia works in partnership with local NGO?s and communities in Uganda, Ethiopia, Ghana, Bolivia, and with Indigenous Peoples in Canada. Kinvia is here with communities who are building local, self-reliant, sustainable systems to provide food for their children, youth, and families across generations. It works in solidarity with communities to impact all areas of nourishment at all stages of their lives, including income generation, education, gender equality, racial justice, and climate impacts. About this opportunity Reporting to the President & Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Revenue & Strategic Partnerships (?VP?) is accountable for advancing its long-term financial sustainability through an integrated, diversified, and partnership-driven revenue strategy aligned with Kinvia?s 10-year strategic directions. As a key member of Kinvia?s Senior Leadership Team, the VP is accountable for the day-to-day operation of the Philanthropy Team and the organization?s annual revenue targets. The VP also advises and supports the President & CEO and the Board to advance Kinvia?s mission and financial sustainability. Mentoring, supporting, and collaborating with a dedicated team, as well as collaborating across teams, the VP ensures donor and constituent relationships are built and stewarded, while providing strategic leadership to the team in executing key initiatives, ensuring vision, growth, and relationship-building are fully realized in practice. Key aspects of this role include revenue generation and diversification, resource mobilization, as well as integrated communications, storytelling, stewardship activities, and brand enablement to ensure that all fundraising communications and engagement strategies effectively support Kinvia?s brand and revenue generation and diversification objectives. Vision A world in which children, youth and their communities thrive, realizing their full potential. Mission Kinvia accompanies children, youth, and their communities as they work to overcome systemic barriers to ensuring their rights to nutritious and culturally appropriate food, fostering wholistic well-being. Kinvia?s Approach Kinvia?s approach is grounded in a community led approach. Kinvia works alongside local partners and communities to support them to achieve self-determined, equitable and sustainable food systems. Our approach also recognizes the importance of working directly or indirectly with the economic, social, environmental and political systems that underpin and influence food systems. Kinvia?s Values Kinvia?s values are how it governs the organization, makes decisions and acts as it undertakes its work together. They also serve as the foundation of its culture, behaviors and core beliefs. Accountability ? Kinvia demonstrates its commitment to trust through responsible actions, a focus on meaningful impact, transparency, and reciprocal accountability. Partnership ? It nurtures collaborative relationships and engages communities in shaping decisions that affect their lives. Inclusiveness ? It diligently works to create safe spaces where diverse perspectives and experiences can inform and direct change. Solidarity ? It uplifts one another and accompany those affected by systems of oppression and marginalization. Respect ? Kinvia values the dignity of people and uphold human rights. Humility ? Kinvia is on a continuous journey of healing, growth and discovery, and are committed to creating spaces where they can listen to and learn from each other. description: Salary Range $100,000 - $150,000 This posting is for an existing vacancy. We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants. The Short Version You'd be our marketing function. Not a marketing team member - the function. One person, senior, with the mandate and the budget to decide what we say, how it looks, and where it runs. That's either the most appealing thing you've read this month or a red flag. We'd rather you know now. Why This Isn't an Agency Job At an agency you'd touch twelve brands and own none of them. Here you own one, end to end: the strategy, the words, the visuals, the campaign, and the number it moved. You'll see a piece of work from a half-idea in a Tuesday meeting through to the metric it changed a quarter later. Very few marketers get that loop, and it's the fastest way we know to get good. You'll report to our Founder, sit close to our Executive Management team, and have real authority over the brand. When you say we're not doing something, we're not doing it. What You'd Actually Do Own the marketing strategy and the budget behind it Write - properly. Editorial, campaign, product, the occasional thing under someone else's name Design and ship the assets. You'll art-direct yourself most of the time Run our content engine end to end: what we publish, why, and whether it works Use AI tooling the way a craftsperson uses a jig - to move faster on the parts that don't need you, so you can spend your judgment where it counts Bring in freelancers and contractors when the work outgrows one pair of hands, and manage them well Tell us honestly what's working and what isn't Who We Think This Is We're looking for an unusual combination, and we know it. You've probably got two of these deeply and can hold your own in the others: Journalism or editorial. You can find the story, ask the uncomfortable question, and structure an argument. You've worked to a deadline that didn't move. Design and graphics. You can build the asset, not just brief it. Figma or Adobe, and taste that shows in the work. AI fluency. You've integrated generative tools into a real workflow and formed opinions about where they help and where they quietly make things worse. Marketing outcomes. You've owned a number, not just a deliverable. Senior-level judgment matters more to us than years. If you've spent three years running a small brand well, that may beat eight years in a large one. This is an entry-level opportunity for a young person who is interested in human rights, social justice, community engagement, campaigning, and movement building. The successful candidate will provide coordination and administrative support to key activism and campaign initiatives, with a particular focus on Amnesty International?s Write for Rights campaign. The role will also support opportunities related to activist engagement, communications, campaign mobilization, digital community engagement, and the implementation of the People Power approach. This position offers an opportunity to gain practical experience in national human rights campaigning while working collaboratively with staff, activists, volunteers, and community partners. WHAT YOU?LL DO Key Responsibilities 1. Write for Rights Campaign Support Support the planning and coordination of Write for Rights activities and initiatives. Assist with tracking campaign activities, events, deadlines, and deliverables. Support communication with activists, volunteers, local groups, and other campaign participants. Assist in preparing campaign resources, materials, and participant communications. Support the collection and organization of campaign participation data and outcomes. Help coordinate follow-up communications with campaign participants. Assist in documenting lessons learned and recommendations following campaign activities. 2. Activist Engagement and Mobilization Support outreach and engagement with activists, volunteers, and supporters. Assist in identifying opportunities to strengthen participation in Amnesty?s campaigns and activism initiatives. Help coordinate online and in-person engagement activities. Support communications related to activism opportunities, events, and calls to action. Assist with maintaining accurate contact lists and engagement records. Help identify and share stories, successes, and examples of activist participation. 3. Campaign and Communications Support Assist with drafting and preparing campaign communications, including emails, newsletters, and social media content. Support the development and organization of campaign resources and toolkits. Assist with internal coordination between Activism, Campaigns, Communications, and other relevant teams. Support research and information gathering related to campaign issues and audiences. Assist with monitoring campaign engagement and identifying emerging trends. 4. People Power and Community Engagement Support initiatives that strengthen community participation and movement engagement. Assist with onboarding and engaging participants in relevant digital community spaces and platforms. Help organize resources and information for activists and community members. Support opportunities for peer learning, collaboration, and knowledge sharing. Assist with gathering feedback from activists and supporters to inform future engagement strategies. 5. Administrative and Coordination Support Support meeting coordination, including scheduling, agendas, notes, and action tracking. Maintain organized campaign files, documents, and shared resources. Assist with event logistics and participant coordination. Support reporting, data collection, and tracking of activities. Undertake other related duties in support of the Activism & Movement Engagement team. WHAT WE?RE LOOKING FOR IN A CANDIDATE The selected candidate is expected to embody and promote the organization?s values of respect, equity, and fairness, contributing to an inclusive, anti-racist, and anti-oppressive work environment at all times. Qualifications and Experience The successful candidate will have: An interest in human rights, social justice, activism, community organizing, or campaigning. Some previous experience through employment, volunteering, internships, student leadership, or community involvement. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational and time-management skills. The ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative team. Experience using Microsoft Office and digital communication tools. An interest in learning about campaigning, mobilization, and movement building. An understanding of or interest in equity, anti-racism, inclusion, and human rights. Asset The following would be considered an asset: Experience volunteering or participating in campaigns or community initiatives. Experience supporting events or community engagement activities. Familiarity with social media and digital communications. Experience working with volunteers or diverse communities. Knowledge of Amnesty International?s human rights work and mission. Experience with data tracking, CRM systems, or digital community platforms. Key Competencies The successful candidate will demonstrate: Commitment to Human Rights: A genuine interest in advancing human rights and social justice. Communication: Ability to communicate clearly and respectfully with diverse audiences. Organization: Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines. Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with staff, volunteers, and community members. Initiative: Willingness to learn, take initiative, and contribute ideas. Equity and Inclusion: Commitment to anti-racism, equity, accessibility, and inclusive practices. Adaptability: Ability to work in a dynamic campaign environment. This is a part-time, five-month contract position , working 25 hours per week at $24.00 per hour . The successful candidate may be required to work occasional evenings or weekends to support campaign events or activism activities, with advance notice and in accordance with organizational policies. APPLICATION PROCESS Applications (resume and cover) must be submitted electronically through out Work With Us careers page. We thank everyone for their expression of interest-and truly appreciative of the time individuals put into applying-but with the limitation of time only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Amnesty International Canada is committed to providing an inclusive and barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs. Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage during the recruitment process

title: Child and Youth Counsellor (School support)
address: 435 James Street South, Thunder Bay, ON, P7E 6T1
description: About the Organization At the Child and Parent Resource Institute (CPRI) we provide highly specialized trauma-informed mental health and developmental services. These services include Assessment, Consultation, Treatment, Research and Education. We work with local community services, building on what they have already done and use evidence based practices to adapt our approach to the unique needs of each child. Position Overview CPRI is looking for Child and Youth Counsellors to provide care and treatment in accordance with the residents' individual treatment program and in liaison with their families and community agencies. These positions will provide school support to the clients. Key Responsibilities Provide care, assessment and treatment in the provision of highly specialized residential treatment services for children and youth with complex mental health issues and/or developmental challenges. Work as part of a multidisciplinary team, involving clinicians, guardians and community resources, to utilize best practices, trauma-informed approaches and using a bio-psycho-social model of care in the treatment of children. Work during any assigned shift, during a 24 hour period to assist clients with normal activities of daily living, recognize and report any physical signs and symptoms of health conditions and provide assessment of clients in accordance to the Plan of Care goals. Following completion of training, administer medications and treatments in accordance with CPRI Medication Procedure. Provide individual care, counselling and group therapy for clients. Identify stages of behavioural escalation and respond in a clinically appropriate manner to deescalate the behaviour and develop strategies to reduce the clients concerning behaviours. Maintain clinical records and documents, actively participate in communication processes with partners and participate in plan of care meetings, etc. Attend regular training and development opportunities to maintain an up-to-date knowledge of safeguarding, health and safety and well-being of children and youth being served. Enhance the social, behavioural and emotional functioning of children and youth within the classroom. Plan, collaborate and implement Individual Crisis Management Plan (ICMP) and individual programs. Utilize and review ICMP strategies and individual programs. Provide feedback to the clinical team and primary counsellors regarding client strengths and barriers regarding implementation of ICMP and individual plans within the school setting. Provide educational staff with information and updates on ICMP and individual programs. Encourage a positive school culture and enhance learning with the teacher and client. Assist in the integration of the child and youth's treatment goals with the classroom program, to further the child and youth's overall treatment progress. Daily documentation on clients in the classroom including data collection as requested by clinical team. Transitioning clients to and from school. Planning and provision of summer programming. Qualifications You have successfully completed the: Child and Youth Worker program, or Developmental Service Worker program, or Equivalent with a minimum of one year's experience in a related field following graduation. Knowledge and Experience You have demonstrated experience providing care and treatment to children with physical, developmental and/or behaviour needs on-site and in the community. You have knowledge of evidence based practices for children and adolescents with developmental delay and/or mental health problems, including behavioural modification strategies, learning theories, counselling skills and clinical practices. You are able to develop and implement individual client treatment plan reviews, program evaluation, and educational programs and knowledge of professional, community and facility resources available to assist the child/family. You are able to safely and effectively manage behavioural crisis situations and respond in a trauma-informed approach. Communication Skills You have effective oral and written communication skills to liaise and consult with relevant team members, and provide counsel to residents, their families and community agencies. Analytical, Assessment, and Problem-Solving Skills You can gather and compile data from multiple sources to identify client needs. You can develop/modify client plans of care. Organizational Skills You can manage conflicting priorities, make appropriate care decisions, and maintain adequate records. Salary: $1,184.70 - $1,336.66 Per week Note: If you have not completed the Medication Training Program, administering medications and treatments as prescribed by a physician and in accordance with the CPRI Medication Procedure, you will be hired in the Child and Youth Assistant (CCW1) salary range ($1,082.59 - $1,195.32 Per Week) until this is successfully completed. Don't meet every qualification? Education Requirement 1 Education Requirement Diploma in Social Services and Public Policy Requirement Are Working Towards or Have Earned Any of the Following: Diploma Studied at least one of the following subject areas: Social Services and Public Policy Preferred year of study: Graduate Preferred Institution Fanshawe College

title: Communications & Capacity Building Coordinator
description: Independent Contractor | Part-Time | Remote / British Columbia Contract Period: November 1, 2026 ? Strong writing, editing, proofreading, and plain-language communication skills. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines independently. Ability to work collaboratively with a range of colleagues, people with lived and/or living experience(s), member organizations, and community partners. Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work. Comfort working independently in a remote environment and proactively communicating about progress, priorities, and challenges. Assets: Experience in public health, health promotion, community-based organizations, HIV, viral hepatitis, STBBIs, harm reduction, sexual health, substance use, or related fields. Experience with knowledge translation or knowledge mobilization. Experience developing adult learning or educational resources. Experience supporting virtual or in-person workshops, webinars, or training. Experience with online learning platforms or learning management systems. Experience with digital communications, social media, email marketing, or website content management. title: Job Developer/Employer Services-Horticulture Employment Program
description: About You As a Job Developer/Employer Services you bring strong employer-engagement, job-development, and relationship-building skills. You understand Ontario?s landscape and horticulture industry and can identify employers? workforce needs, develop employment opportunities, and communicate the value of hiring GROW participants. You are proactive, results-focused, and comfortable building new relationships through outreach, site visits, industry events, and ongoing follow-up. You can manage multiple employer relationships and placement opportunities while maintaining accurate records and working toward defined employment and retention targets. What You?ll Be Doing You will build and maintain relationships with landscape and horticulture employers, develop paid employment and training placement opportunities, and connect employers with qualified GROW participants. You will drive employer outreach, recruitment activities, workforce planning support, hiring incentives, placement monitoring, and employer-focused retention strategies. Working closely with participant-facing staff, you will help create strong employment matches and achieve GROW?s employer engagement, placement, and retention targets. What You?ll Be Responsible For Employer Engagement and Job Development: Recruit and engage landscape and horticulture employers across Ontario. Build and maintain an active portfolio of employer relationships and employment opportunities. Conduct employer outreach through calls, meetings, site visits, industry events, chapter and sector activities, and referrals. Assess employers? workforce needs, hiring requirements, workplace environments, and available positions. Promote the benefits of hiring GROW participants, engage and support employers with apprenticeship registration, sponsorship and workforce development, and encourage inclusive, barrier-free recruitment practices. Position Landscape Ontario and GROW as trusted workforce-development partners for the industry. Maintain regular contact with employers to identify current and future workforce needs. Employment and Placement Matching: Match GROW participants with suitable registered employers based on participant qualifications, employment goals, employer needs, and workplace fit. Develop paid employment, work-experience, and Training Placement Agreement opportunities for GROW participants. Gather accurate information about job duties, qualifications, schedules, compensation, workplace expectations, and advancement opportunities. Work with the Employment & Career Development Coordinator and other program staff to identify suitable candidates. Coordinate employer introductions, interviews, hiring activities, and placement documentation. Support employers in understanding applicable hiring incentives, wage subsidies, and program requirements. Ensure placement opportunities meet GROW and Ministry requirements. Conduct employer and workplace monitoring visits when required. Employer Support and Retention: Support employers throughout recruitment, onboarding, placement, and retention. Help employers address workplace integration, communication, performance, and retention challenges. Provide employer-focused coaching, practical resources, and referrals to relevant Landscape Ontario services. Liaise with participant-facing staff when an employment issue requires coordinated support. Identify risks early and help develop appropriate strategies to support successful employment outcomes. Gather employer feedback to improve participant preparation, training, placement quality, and program delivery. Employer Initiatives and Industry Outreach: Recruit employer participation for hiring events, job fairs, information sessions, workshops, and industry events. Recruit employers to participate in GROW?s Employer of Choice (EOC) initiative and support ongoing EOC employer engagement. Deliver or support employer-focused training related to recruitment, onboarding, retention, and workforce planning. Represent GROW and Landscape Ontario at chapter meetings, sector meetings, trade events, career fairs, and networking activities. Develop relationships with industry associations, community partners, Employment Ontario providers, and other workforce-development organizations. Share employer and labour-market insights with the GROW team to support recruitment, training, and service planning. Performance, Records and Reporting: Deliver shared employer engagement, placement, employment, and retention targets. Maintain accurate employer profiles, job opportunities, site visits, participant matches, placements, and follow-up records. Ensure Training Placement Agreements and related documentation are complete, accurate, and submitted on time. Monitor progress and provide updates on employer pipelines, participant matches, employment outcomes, risks, and required follow-up. Support internal and funder reporting by maintaining complete and reliable program records. Contribute to team planning and continuous improvement based on employer and participant outcomes. Requirements Experience in employer engagement, job development, recruitment, workforce development, business development, or employment services. Ability and willingness to travel throughout Ontario for employer visits, industry events, hiring fairs, and other program activities, including occasional overnight stays. Strong knowledge of Ontario?s landscape and horticulture industry, including its employers, occupations, workforce needs, and seasonal operations. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain employer relationships. Experience developing employment opportunities and supporting job matching, placements, or retention. Ability to work effectively with employers and participants throughout the employment process. Strong communication, presentation, negotiation, coaching, and relationship-building skills. Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple employers, participants, opportunities, and deadlines. Experience maintaining accurate records and tracking progress against established targets. Proficiency with digital collaboration, database, and program-management tools. Ability to work independently, take initiative, solve problems, and collaborate across teams. Experience with Employment Ontario, Ministry-funded programs, hiring incentives, wage subsidies, or Training Placement Agreements is an asset. A valid Ontario driver?s licence and access to reliable transportation are required. About this position Full-time, fixed-term contract position through June 29, 2027, with the possibility of renewal. Two positions are available. Salary: $65,000 - $75,000 (depending on experience) Includes vacation and personal time off, and health benefits. Reports to the Workforce Development Manager and works closely with the Employment & Career Development Coordinator and other GROW staff. Landscape Ontario has a hybrid work model in place allowing for flexibility and fluidity in your weekly schedule. Some evening or weekend work will be required based on program activities and events. Regular travel within Ontario is required for employer visits, placements, training activities, and events. A supportive, collaborative team environment. A beautifully renovated modern office space. Our office is in Milton, ON at the 401 between James Snow Parkway and Trafalgar Rd. About Landscape Ontario Landscape Ontario Horticultural Trades Association is a provincial trade association representing approximately 2,600+ members across the landscape horticulture sector. A not-for-profit, volunteer-driven organization, we are dedicated to advancing the profession through leadership, education and collaboration. Landscape Ontario members design, build and maintain outdoor spaces that support healthy communities, environmental resilience and economic growth across Ontario. We are committed to building an inclusive and collaborative organization where everyone feels welcomed and valued, regardless of gender, race, nationality, orientation or ability. title: Programs Specialist
description: Programs Specialist Reports to Senior Director of Member Programs Location Remote work from anywhere in Canada Salary $62,000 - $68,000 About CanREA The Canadian Renewable Energy Association (CanREA) is the voice for wind energy, solar energy and energy storage in Canada. We represent 350+ member companies working to advance the policies, regulations and market conditions that will power Canada?s clean energy future. Our work spans advocacy, research, events and member services, all in service of a more sustainable electricity system for Canada and future generations. Learn more at renewablesassociation.ca. The Role The Program Specialist provides scheduling, logistics and coordination support across CanREA's Programs Team portfolio, which spans operational best practices, site health and safety, workforce development, insurance best practices, advocacy for behind-the-meter solar and energy storage, statistics and data analysis. Success in this role means that meetings, committees and working groups are scheduled accurately and run smoothly, that stakeholders receive timely, professional outreach and consistent follow-up, and that program files and action items stay organized and on track. The position reports to the Senior Director of Member Programs and works closely with the Manager of Programs and Programs Team colleagues to keep project files moving day to day. Externally, the Program Specialist communicates regularly with member companies, provincial and territorial associations, colleges, polytechnics and other training institutions, unions and training providers, Indigenous organizations, and sector councils to schedule meetings, confirm availability and attendance, and follow up on outstanding items. Primary Responsibilities Calendar and Meeting Scheduling Coordinate and maintain calendars for Programs Team meetings, committees, working groups and task forces, confirming availability across internal and external participants and time zones. Schedule recurring and ad hoc meetings using scheduling and calendar tools (e.g., MS Outlook, Monday.com, or equivalent) and arrange video conference links. Prepare and circulate meeting agendas and pre-read materials in advance of scheduled sessions. Record decisions, action items and next steps during meetings, and distribute minutes promptly after each session. Stakeholder Outreach and Follow-Up Conduct outreach by phone and email to member companies, training institutions, government contacts and other external stakeholders to confirm meeting attendance and gather scheduling availability. Follow up with assigned owners on outstanding action items to confirm completion by agreed deadlines, escalating to the Manager or Senior Director where needed. Maintain up-to-date contact lists and distribution groups for member committees, working groups, training partners and other Programs Team stakeholders. Respond promptly and professionally to stakeholder inquiries, directing more complex questions to the appropriate Programs Team lead. Program and Project Coordination Support the Programs Team in tracking workplans, timelines and deliverables across the portfolio, including wind, solar and energy storage operational best practices, site health and safety, workforce development, insurance best practices, and behind-themeter solar and energy storage advocacy. Maintain organized project files, shared drives and tracking documents so that program status is current and easy for the team to access. Coordinate the logistics of producing and circulating technical guidance, best-practice documents and position papers, including formatting, proofreading support and version control. description: Delivery Program Assistant Parkdale Community Food Bank Department: Delivery Program Location: In-Person (5 Brock Avenue, Toronto) Employment Type: Part-Time 16 - 20 hours per week. Thursday - Saturday. Rate: $27.20 per hour This is an existing vacancy. We are currently seeking the ideal candidate to join our Delivery Team as the Delivery Program Assistant. This position supports our delivery program in a variety of ways, including inventory management assistance, supervising volunteers, working with the drop-in team to maximize efficiencies and supporting pick ups and deliveries on a daily basis. If this sounds like the right position for you, please see details and application instructions below. Who We Are Parkdale Community Food Bank (PCFB) is a non-profit, registered charity in the heart of Toronto?s Parkdale neighbourhood. Every month, our programs support more than 17,000 individuals with access to nutritious food and community support. We believe joy is fundamental to nourishment, and our mission is to create a hunger-free community where everyone has a place at our table, with barrier-free access to food they actually want to eat. About the Delivery Program PCFB founded one of the first completely free grocery delivery programs in Toronto back in 2020, to reach community members who couldn?t leave their homes during the pandemic. The program has kept going since, now serving people who face mobility or health barriers to visiting the food bank in person. Clients place weekly orders based on what?s available, and this role is what makes sure those orders actually reach their door. Mission of This Role For a lot of our Delivery Program clients, the Delivery Program Assistant is the only person from PCFB they?ll see face to face. The Delivery Program Assistant brings more than groceries. They carry our mission of dignity and joy in nourishment straight to someone?s door, often noticing the small things, a favourite snack, a treat someone mentioned once, that turns a simple delivery into a moment of real care. When a client isn?t able to come to the food bank, you make sure the food bank still comes to them. This role reports to the Delivery Program Manager for daily operations. They split their time between the road (pickups and deliveries) and the warehouse (prepping, sorting, and organizing donations for the team), with the exact mix shifting depending on the season and what the program needs that week. Responsibilities Operations Pick up donations around the Toronto area, coordinated by the Delivery Program Manager. Deliver groceries to community members enrolled in the Delivery Program, including covering driver routes over the summer when the team needs extra hands. Adjust pace and planning around seasonal volume shifts. Winter is the busiest stretch for deliveries (50%+ above baseline), and pickups spike heavily over the holidays. Resource and Donation Management Prepare incoming resource donations for the packing team, sorting through boxes and flagging what goes to Delivery versus Drop-In. Set aside high-value or requested items like coffee, condiments, and treats, for the clients who?d appreciate them most, drawing on knowledge built through packing and client audits. Receive and organize food donations, including sorting Daily Bread Food Bank deliveries and setting aside specialty items for volunteers to pack. Keep the warehouse shelves organized and restocked throughout each shift so packing volunteers can find what they need quickly. Track incoming donations in the team?s Discord channel. Volunteer and Community Support Support volunteers who need a hand across the warehouse, kitchen, drop-in, or delivery team. Answer phones and greet visitors, directing them to the right person or resource. Build relationships with clients through the client audit process, one of the more regular points of direct client contact in this role. Qualifications Must-Haves A valid G driver?s licence and comfort navigating Toronto for pickups and deliveries. Experience in a customer-facing role; regularly interacting with clients and volunteers The ability to juggle multiple moving pieces at once and stay highly organized. Comfort being the visible face of PCFB in the community, including appearing in photos donors sometimes take during pickups Nice-to-Haves Familiarity with Toronto?s food donation and supplier landscape Experience or training related to workplace health and safety Comfort using Discord or similar team communication tools AI is not used at any stage of our hiring process. title: Communications Coordinator
description: British Columbia Council for International Cooperation Job Posting Communications Coordinator Location: This is a remote, work-from-home position based in the Lower Mainland that requires you to attend periodic in-person meetings, retreats and events, largely in Vancouver. Hours: 37.5 hours per week Start date: October 13, 2026 Pay: $67,000-71,000 a year Benefits: After 3 months of employment, extended health benefits are available Application deadline: September 7, 2026 at 11:59pm PT About Us At the British Columbia Council for International Cooperation (BCCIC), we believe that the way we work is as important as the work we do. BCCIC is a membership network that brings together civil society organizations and individuals committed to advancing global justice and contributing to a more just, equitable and sustainable world. Rooted in British Columbia and connected through relationships across Canada and around the world, our members and partners reflect a rich diversity of cultures, languages, histories, identities and ways of knowing. We believe this diversity is one of our greatest sources of learning, creativity and collective wisdom. As a membership organization, our role is to create the conditions for people and organizations to learn from one another, strengthen relationships, navigate complexity together and take collective action. Our team works in a culture of trust, responsibility, shared stewardship and continuous learning. We believe that strong systems support people, learning, collaboration and accountability. We encourage initiative, work across roles toward shared goals, and recognize that everyone contributes not only through their own work but also by helping strengthen the organization as a whole. About the Position The Communications Coordinator helps shape how BCCIC communicates with its members, partners and the broader public. At BCCIC, communications are woven throughout the organization rather than existing as a separate function. The Communications Coordinator works alongside colleagues to strengthen how BCCIC communicates in order to foster understanding, participation and dialogue?supporting member engagement, helping translate complex ideas into accessible language, coordinating communications across the organization, and ensuring that BCCIC's public voice reflects its mission, values and strategic priorities. The role is not simply about communicating BCCIC's work. It is about helping people understand one another, make meaning together and strengthen relationships across a diverse network. Success in this role depends as much on listening as on communicating, and as much on curiosity as on expertise. Our communications serve three interconnected purposes: strengthening relationships across our network, engaging the broader public, and contributing to conversations that advance global justice. Specific Duties: Manage BCCIC's communications to maintain a consistent, accessible, and engaging public presence across all communication channels. Create and manage communication assets and campaigns to support BCCIC initiatives, programs, events and promotions. Plan, write, schedule, and publish social media content while monitoring engagement and responding as appropriate. Maintain and update the BCCIC website to ensure information is current, accurate, and accessible. Coordinate the publication of communications across digital platforms to ensure timely and consistent messaging. Support member and public engagement through targeted communications, announcements, and promotional materials. Develop, write, edit, and distribute regular newsletters, member emails, and other communications. Develop communications that increase public understanding of BCCIC's work and encourage public engagement. Identify communication opportunities by gathering stories, program updates, member achievements, and organizational news for publication. Edit written content for clarity, accessibility, consistency, and alignment with BCCIC's brand and communications standards. Assist with administrative matters related to Communications and Engagement Assist with the planning, promotion, and delivery of public engagement activities, events, webinars, and other organizational initiatives. Provide communications support for events, including promotional campaigns, registration materials, and post-event communications. Monitor and manage the organization's general information inbox and voicemail, responding to inquiries or directing them to the appropriate staff member. Monitor for coherent communications and learning Monitor current events, sector developments, and relevant news to identify resources, stories, and opportunities for BCCIC to share with members and the public. Contribute to BCCIC's Planning, Monitoring, Learning and Accountability (PMLA) processes by documenting communications activities, capturing lessons learned, and advancing continuous improvement by integrating outcomes and metrics from communication initiatives into future iterations. Track communications metrics and engagement data to help evaluate the effectiveness of communications activities and inform future planning. Collaborate with staff, members, partners, and external stakeholders to gather content and support organizational communications. Perform other communications, administrative, and project-related duties as assigned to support the goals of the organization. Technical or Professional Experience Our ideal candidate has: Post-secondary degree in communications, public relations, social justice, international development or another related field Experience with intercultural communications and working collaboratively with diverse actors that may have different views, perspectives, priorities, or goals. 3-5 years of experience working in communications, media, or public relations, ideally experience with BC-based communities Demonstrated proficiency in WordPress, MailChimp, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, SEO, Google Suite, social media analytics, and social and emerging digital media platforms and tools Proven ability to establish and maintain positive, strategic working relationships with key stakeholders and decision-makers Excellent time management, decision making, organizational, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills Demonstrated self-starter who exhibits flexibility, creativity, and initiative Comfortable working with minimal supervision in a deadline-oriented environment Superior written, oral, and online communication skills Experience with public engagement through digital communications and social media Shows a keen attention to detail We May Be a Good Fit for Each Other If... You can work independently, ask good questions, make recommendations, keep our communications active while drawing on contributions from the rest of the team. You are systematic, organized, able to multi-task and accept that there are always moving pieces. You are curious about how people engage with information today and the emerging communications strategies, platforms, practices, and technologies. You understand the importance of timely, relevant and fit-for-purpose communications. You have an understanding of, and enthusiasm for, intercultural communication, with experience communicating with diverse communities and audiences. You enjoy making sense of complexity and are committed to learning with others. What You'll Bring We recognize that excellent candidates bring different combinations of education and experience. You may have experience in communications, journalism, public engagement, public affairs, nonprofit communications or a related field. Experience working with member-based organizations, networks, coalitions or collaborative initiatives will be considered a strong asset. You bring both professional expertise and the perspective that comes from your own lived experiences. We value people who have learned by navigating different contexts, communities, cultures, identities or ways of working, and who draw on those experiences with humility and curiosity. You combine maturity with imagination, understand both systems and relationships, and recognize that practice shapes systems just as much as systems shape practice. Ultimately, we're looking for someone who communicates with clarity, listens with curiosity, exercises good judgment, builds strong relationships, and is excited by the opportunity to help a diverse network learn, connect and act together. How the Team Works This is a full-time remote, work-from-home position based in the lower mainland that requires you to attend in person meetings occasionally. There is an expectation that staff be available for periodic in-person meetings, retreats and events, largely in Vancouver. Everyone at BCCIC, from interns to staff to Board of Directors, are accountable to BCCIC?s strategic directions, its vision, mission and purpose, as well as the Istanbul Principles. You can learn more about these here . We are a flexible, accommodating and supportive team that recognizes that we each work differently, have different needs, and that work is one of the many dimensions of our lives. Given that our team is lean, collaborative and dynamic, all staff are expected to be flexible with their roles and fulfill necessary administrative functions and other tasks deemed necessary What can you expect from the team? A welcoming, inclusive team that is open to difficult discussions and feedback. Experience working within a team that is learning to work in a feminist way, and is learning to use anti-oppressive, anti-racist and decolonized approaches in all aspects of our work, with an international lens. A dynamic group that wants to learn and grow with you. This is a full-time position based on 37.5 hours a week. The salary range for this position is $67,000-71,000 a year. Health insurance is available after 3 months. How to Apply We are accepting applications until September 7, 2026 at 11:59pm PT. The position will start October 13, 2026. To apply, please email BCCIC at info@bccic.ca a brief cover letter and your resume; please include the subject line: Communications Coordinator Application. BCCIC is committed to building a team that reflects the richness and diversity of the communities with whom we work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, cultures, languages and lived experiences, and from those whose life or work has required them to navigate different worlds with openness, curiosity and respect. 3 - 5 years of experience

title: Union Representative
address: Richmond Hill, ON, L4C
description: SEIU Healthcare is a union of more than 67,000 members who are frontline healthcare workers in hospitals, long-term care facilities, and homecare agencies in communities throughout Ontario. We advocate with our members by launching progressive member driven programs, adapting best practices, and encouraging new and innovative ideas. We strive to create a society where workers are valued and rewarded for their work. As a result, thriving workers have a greater opportunity to participate and lead in building healthy communities. We provide a strong voice through collective bargaining, labour relations, and political action to ensure frontline workers are heard and respected when decisions about healthcare are being made. We are looking for individuals with a desire to amplify the voice of workers. If you are passionate about labour and social justice, share our values, and want to work toward changing the lives of workers, then a career with SEIU Healthcare is for you! For more information, visit www.seiuhealthcare.ca . POSITION DESCRIPTION : The Union Representative delivers excellent member service and is responsible for all aspects of labor relations and member engagement in the workplaces they represent. These duties include the effective administration of collective agreements, contract negotiations, grievances, and other matters related to the employment relationship between our members and their employers. The position is also responsible for identifying and coaching member leaders to become more active and capable members of the union and to support our member education and mobilization programs in support of our broader organizational strategy to strengthen a wider movement for social justice and political participation across our membership. This position is a full-time role based at our Mural office in Richmond Hill, Ontario . DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Plan, develop and execute initiatives to encourage member driven unit events, actions, and campaigns to resolve unit issues. Coach stewards to lead various meetings and support SEIU Healthcare in early identification and resolution of unit issues. Support organizational political strategies by recruiting member leaders and promoting and participating in political actions and events. Develop and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders (employers, members, internal departments, OLRB, arbitrators etc.). Facilitate and coordinate General Membership Meetings, Steward Meetings, Labour Management Meetings, Site Visits, and Departmental Meetings in assigned units. Lead collective bargaining for assigned units while working with the Research Department in accordance with established standards, procedures, and timelines. Manage the grievance process, working toward early resolution in accordance with individual collective agreements and internal processes. Analyze and interpret complex contracts and legislative language. Resolve issues within units through interpretation and enforcement of contracts and related legislation. Work in collaboration with administrative support to ensure unit files, unit events, negotiation files, records, reports, and grievance collateral are entered in UnionWare. Facilitate attendance management and return to work meetings in assigned units. Ensure timely submission and preparation of detailed files for interest and rights arbitrations. Ensure required committees in assigned units have SEIU representation. Complete and submit monthly unit status reports and monthly expense reports. Ensure legal and other billing accurately reflects events as they occur and are submitted per policy. Manage and record expenses made during regular business using a company credit card/gas card, in accordance with SEIU financial policies. Other duties as assigned. EDUCATION BACKGROUND At SEIU Healthcare, we understand that the best people do not always have the same access and opportunities to education, and while post-secondary education is always preferred, we want to make sure nothing stands in the way of finding the right person. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED Minimum of three (3) years labour relations experience, preferably in a labor union environment. Experience negotiating first and renewal collective agreements and administer those agreements through their life cycle. Experience handling and processing grievances through referral to arbitration Experience in the healthcare sector is an added advantage SKILLS & COMPETENCIES REQUIRED: Proficiency in languages other than English is an asset. IT skills is an asset Working knowledge of relevant legislation (ESA, OHRC, WSIA, OHSA, OLRA). Ability to interpret collective agreement language and apply to specific situations. Ability to negotiate first and renewal collective agreements and administer those agreements through their life cycle. Ability to process grievances through referral to arbitration Proficient with Microsoft Office and Union Ware Strong interpersonal skills, excellent writing, and verbal skills Strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Strong conflict resolution skills and the ability to deal with tense situations. Self-motivated and able to work independently with minimal supervision. Time management skills. Building and maintaining trust relationships with all stakeholders. OTHER REQUIREMENTS This position requires the successful candidate to have a valid driver's license. The successful candidate would have to provide proof that s/he has a valid driver's license upon being hired. PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ WORKING CONDITIONS / ENVIRONMENT Office work may involve prolonged periods of sitting at a workstation and repetitive movements associated with such tasks. Field work may involve extended periods away from home, long hours, and exposure to both physically and mentally demanding environments. Evening and weekend work may be required. Work hours will vary to meet operational needs. Prolonged use of a computer. Frequent use of the telephone. Driving, air travel, cross-border travel, and attendance at off-site meetings. Frequent long-distance travel by motor vehicle. Must be able to lift and transport boxes containing various materials to and from meetings. Exposure to medical, healthcare, and office environments How to Apply Written applications that detail your qualifications and experience should be submitted on our career portal . Salary and other terms and conditions are in accordance with the field staff collective agreement. Please note that the Employer reserves the right to transfer or assign staff anywhere within the SEIU Local 1 Canada jurisdiction.
